Title: Martin MacInnes: Deep Oceans and Deep Space
Teaser: Sometimes a book lands on earth perfectly formed, as if from another planet. Edinburgh-based Martin MacInnes’ third novel, In Ascension, takes readers on a journey to the outer reaches of the imagination, with searching questions about the...
Description: Sometimes a book lands on earth perfectly formed, as if from another planet. Edinburgh-based Martin MacInnes’ third novel, In Ascension, takes readers on a journey to the outer reaches of the imagination, with searching questions about the surprisingly blurred boundaries between humans and the rest of the universe. Moving, mind-expanding, and beautifully written, this novel announces MacInnes as a star of Scottish literature. In converstation with Stuart Kelly.

Title: Merryn Glover & Rachel Hewitt: Women in the Wild
Teaser: Recent years have seen a seismic shift in nature writing. Join two authors who entwine historical narratives of courageous women with their own experiences of the great outdoors. Merryn Glover’s The Hidden Fires presents new understandings of the...
Description: Recent years have seen a seismic shift in nature writing. Join two authors who entwine historical narratives of courageous women with their own experiences of the great outdoors. Merryn Glover’s The Hidden Fires presents new understandings of the Cairngorms, while Rachel Hewitt’s In Her Nature explores how running through landscape recovered a sense of belonging after grief. In this innovative event, hear them in conversation with endurance cyclist Emily Chappell, then join them for a special hike the following day. For place limits and more details see edbookfest.co.uk/insideout.

Title: Jackie Kay: A Life in Protest
Teaser: At the centre of her forthcoming poetry collection, A Life in Protest, Jackie Kay has produced a landmark poem of the same name which charts a powerful and moving poetic journey back through key moments of political activism in her life. As the Book...
Description: At the centre of her forthcoming poetry collection, A Life in Protest, Jackie Kay has produced a landmark poem of the same name which charts a powerful and moving poetic journey back through key moments of political activism in her life. As the Book Festival celebrates its 40th anniversary, Kay shares this new poem and some of the others in her collection, and looks back over key events in her life as a writer. In conversation with Hannah Lavery.

Title: Dionne Brand: No Language is Neutral
Teaser: One of Canada’s most honoured poets visits Edinburgh to discuss Nomenclature: New and Collected Poems, newly issued as a Penguin Modern Classic. Combining the titular new long poem with work from her lauded 40 year career, Brand’s poetry is an...
Description: One of Canada’s most honoured poets visits Edinburgh to discuss Nomenclature: New and Collected Poems, newly issued as a Penguin Modern Classic. Combining the titular new long poem with work from her lauded 40 year career, Brand’s poetry is an incisive exploration of race, sexuality, moral hypocrisies, migration, and exile, executed with spectacular imagination and formal mastery. In conversation with Alycia Pirmohamed.

Title: Ned Boulting: Cyclists on Celluloid
Teaser: Ned Boulting is one of the UK’s best-known voices of cycling. In 2020, Boulting bought a two-minute length of ageing Pathé news film, featuring a stage of the 1923 Tour de France race. He undertook an investigation of every frame: a journey of...
Description: Ned Boulting is one of the UK’s best-known voices of cycling. In 2020, Boulting bought a two-minute length of ageing Pathé news film, featuring a stage of the 1923 Tour de France race. He undertook an investigation of every frame: a journey of discovery about France and the mysterious men who raced a century ago. 1923 is the captivating result which he discusses today with long-distance cyclist Emily Chappell.

Title: Anahit Behrooz & Eris Young: 'Just' Friends
Teaser: How can we resist the popular notion that romance is the only road to intimacy? Anahit Behrooz and Eris Young have some empowering ideas. Behrooz's BFFs is a celebration of the complexities and pleasures of female friendship as seen in popular culture,...
Description: How can we resist the popular notion that romance is the only road to intimacy? Anahit Behrooz and Eris Young have some empowering ideas. Behrooz's BFFs is a celebration of the complexities and pleasures of female friendship as seen in popular culture, and Young's Ace Voices represents a multitude of true stories and life lessons from people across the asexual and aromantic spectrum. Chaired by Kevin Guyan.

Title: Kirsty Logan & Johanne Lykke Holm: Witches, Power and the Patriarchy
Teaser: In her latest novel, Now She is Witch, Scottish writer, poet, and performer Kirsty Logan grapples with what power and freedom can mean in a patriarchal world. In Strega, Swedish author Johanne Lykke Holm explores the potency and violence of age-long...
Description: In her latest novel, Now She is Witch, Scottish writer, poet, and performer Kirsty Logan grapples with what power and freedom can mean in a patriarchal world. In Strega, Swedish author Johanne Lykke Holm explores the potency and violence of age-long myths. Together, these two writers join forces to explore why the figure of the witch continues to speak to the plight of marginalised people today.

Title: Isabella Tree: How to Rewild the World
Teaser: In The Book of Wilding, co-written with her husband, conservationist Charlie Burrell, Isabella Tree continues where the bestselling Wilding left off by sharing more practical insights from the landmark rewilding project at Knepp Estate. The enormity of...
Description: In The Book of Wilding, co-written with her husband, conservationist Charlie Burrell, Isabella Tree continues where the bestselling Wilding left off by sharing more practical insights from the landmark rewilding project at Knepp Estate. The enormity of climate change and biodiversity loss can feel overwhelming, but Tree is uniquely placed to provide us with tangible answers and practical solutions. In conversation with Sophie Cunningham.

Title: Brian Dillon & Brandon Taylor: Essay Means ‘To Try’
Teaser: Difficult to define and diverse by its nature, the essay is a slippery form. It requires – according to Brian Dillon – some 'combination of exactitude and evasion'. Join Dillon, author of a new collection of interlinked essays, Affinities, alongside...
Description: Difficult to define and diverse by its nature, the essay is a slippery form. It requires – according to Brian Dillon – some 'combination of exactitude and evasion'. Join Dillon, author of a new collection of interlinked essays, Affinities, alongside Booker Prize-shortlisted author, critic, and essayist, Brandon Taylor as they discuss the form, function, and very point of the genre with Michael Williams.

Title: Jenny Erpenbeck: Old World Evaporates
Teaser: ‘You can’t forget what it felt like to be on the other side of history,’ said Jenny Erpenbeck about one ‘experiential advantage’ of growing up in former East Germany. Hear Erpenbeck, one of Europe's greatest living writers, talking about her...
Description: ‘You can’t forget what it felt like to be on the other side of history,’ said Jenny Erpenbeck about one ‘experiential advantage’ of growing up in former East Germany. Hear Erpenbeck, one of Europe's greatest living writers, talking about her novel Kairos: the story of a manipulative relationship between a young woman and an older man which functions as a fascinating metaphor for life under a decaying, controlling regime. In conversation with Jenny Niven.

Title: Ian McEwan: The Measure of a Life
Teaser: It’s been described as ‘a tour de force’ and ‘one of the finest humanist novels of its age’. Without doubt, Ian McEwan’s Lessons is a towering achievement by one of Britain’s greatest living writers. In today’s session, he discusses how...
Description: It’s been described as ‘a tour de force’ and ‘one of the finest humanist novels of its age’. Without doubt, Ian McEwan’s Lessons is a towering achievement by one of Britain’s greatest living writers. In today’s session, he discusses how much of himself he has woven into his novel, and about the tsunami of 20th century history that carries along his thoughtful protagonist Roland Baines. In conversation with Kirsty Wark.

Title: Hashi Mohamed: Right to Home
Teaser: Hashi Mohamed has wowed readers with his insightful writing about social mobility in the UK. His latest book, A Home of One’s Own, has been proclaimed ‘a marvel’ by Philippe Sands. As a top planning barrister who came to Britain as a child...
Description: Hashi Mohamed has wowed readers with his insightful writing about social mobility in the UK. His latest book, A Home of One’s Own, has been proclaimed ‘a marvel’ by Philippe Sands. As a top planning barrister who came to Britain as a child refugee, today Mohamed shares his acute personal awareness and professional knowledge about the housing crisis and his perspective on how to fix it. In conversation with Humza Yousaf.

Title: Jenny Erpenbeck & Katja Hoyer: East Germany – Beyond the Myths
Teaser: Prior to the fall of the Berlin Wall and reunification, East Germany was regarded in western democracies as a ruthless surveillance machine under the auspices of the dreaded Stasi. But, as historian Katya Hoyer shows in her counterintuitive study,...
Description: Prior to the fall of the Berlin Wall and reunification, East Germany was regarded in western democracies as a ruthless surveillance machine under the auspices of the dreaded Stasi. But, as historian Katya Hoyer shows in her counterintuitive study, Beyond the Wall, citizens enjoyed full employment and a reasonable standard of living. Join Hoyer in conversation with leading German novelist Jenny Erpenbeck, who also grew up in the East and whose writing has been deeply informed by the experience. Chaired by Nick Barley.

Title: Raynor Winn: A Walk on the Wild Side
Teaser: In The Salt Path, Raynor Winn told the story of a healing walk on the South West Coast Path with her unwell husband, Moth. Winn’s third book, Landlines, recounts Raynor and Moth’s most ambitious walk yet – an epic 1,000-mile journey starting with...
Description: In The Salt Path, Raynor Winn told the story of a healing walk on the South West Coast Path with her unwell husband, Moth. Winn’s third book, Landlines, recounts Raynor and Moth’s most ambitious walk yet – an epic 1,000-mile journey starting with the Cape Wrath trail and ending in Cornwall. Crystalline nature writing shot through with compassion and humour, this is literature for those who wander. In conversation with Claire Urquhart.

Title: Eleanor Catton: Green is The Colour of Money
Teaser: If Eleanor Catton’s new novel, Birnam Wood, is an echo of Shakespeare’s ‘Scottish Play’... who represents Macbeth? Just one of the enjoyable puzzles of this compulsive and wildly entertaining thriller. Her previous outing, The Luminaries,...
Description: If Eleanor Catton’s new novel, Birnam Wood, is an echo of Shakespeare’s ‘Scottish Play’... who represents Macbeth? Just one of the enjoyable puzzles of this compulsive and wildly entertaining thriller. Her previous outing, The Luminaries, scooped up the Booker Prize, making Catton the youngest winner in its history. Now she’s back with a story asking searching questions about New Zealand and its attitudes to money and technology. In conversation with Nicola Sturgeon.

Title: From Page To Screen: Mayflies
Teaser: Andrew O’Hagan’s Mayflies is an achingly moving account of friendship and loss – and now a celebrated screen adaptation. O’Hagan is joined by two members of the production team: screenwriter Andrea Gibb and executive producer of Synchronicity...
Description: Andrew O’Hagan’s Mayflies is an achingly moving account of friendship and loss – and now a celebrated screen adaptation. O’Hagan is joined by two members of the production team: screenwriter Andrea Gibb and executive producer of Synchronicity Films, Claire Mundell, to talk about the creative journey of adapting the novel. Chaired by Hannah Griffiths, head of literary acquisitions at All3Media.

Title: Polly Morland, Annabel Sowemimo & Phil Whitaker: Prescriptions for Health
Teaser: 2023: the 75th anniversary of the NHS, a vital part of our lives under constant threat. Three authors join us to discuss the challenges facing the system. Polly Morland’s profile of a country doctor, A Fortunate Woman, emphasises the importance of...
Description: 2023: the 75th anniversary of the NHS, a vital part of our lives under constant threat. Three authors join us to discuss the challenges facing the system. Polly Morland’s profile of a country doctor, A Fortunate Woman, emphasises the importance of medicine in regional communities; Dr Annabel Sowemimo’s Divided argues for the decolonisation of healthcare; and Dr Phil Whitaker’s What Is a Doctor? offers a roadmap for the future of the NHS. Chaired by Sarah Brown.

Title: Sophie Duncan & Isabelle Schuler: Rethinking Shakespeare
Teaser: 400 years after the publication of his first Folio, two writers discuss how the legacy of Shakespearean characters endures. In Searching for Juliet, Sophie Duncan reveals the surprising story behind Shakespeare's tragic heroine: from enslaved people in...
Description: 400 years after the publication of his first Folio, two writers discuss how the legacy of Shakespearean characters endures. In Searching for Juliet, Sophie Duncan reveals the surprising story behind Shakespeare's tragic heroine: from enslaved people in the Caribbean and Italian fascists in Verona to real-life lovers in Afghanistan. Isabelle Schuler’s Lady MacBethad gives Shakespeare’s Macbeth a new origin story. There’s no question that this event is the place to be. Chaired by Robyn Marsack.

Title: Isabel Waidner: Prize Writer
Teaser: Isabel Waidner won the Goldsmiths Prize for Sterling Karat Gold, a radical satire of the British justice system. We welcome Waidner back to the Festival with their latest novel, Corey Fah Does Social Mobility, a radiant and revolutionary tale about...
Description: Isabel Waidner won the Goldsmiths Prize for Sterling Karat Gold, a radical satire of the British justice system. We welcome Waidner back to the Festival with their latest novel, Corey Fah Does Social Mobility, a radiant and revolutionary tale about the pitfalls of social mobility and literary prizes. Join Waidner for an exploration of wormholes, time loops, and reality TV. In conversation with Harry Josephine Giles.

Title: Kate Mosse: Romance And Revenge On The Barbary Coast
Teaser: There can’t be many people who have had a more positive impact on women writers than Kate Mosse. As well as being the founder of the Women’s Prize for Fiction, she’s the bestselling author of historical novels in which women are resolutely on top....
Description: There can’t be many people who have had a more positive impact on women writers than Kate Mosse. As well as being the founder of the Women’s Prize for Fiction, she’s the bestselling author of historical novels in which women are resolutely on top. Today she discusses The Ghost Ship: a tale of love, vengeance, and breathtaking peril on the high seas, with Val McDermid.

Title: Jennifer Robinson & Keina Yoshida: Beyond Reasonable Doubt
Teaser: How Many More Women? exposes a rising threat to survivors of gender-based violence who want to speak out against abuse: the legal teams of powerful men who suppress allegations and prevent newspapers from running stories. Join renowned human rights...
Description: How Many More Women? exposes a rising threat to survivors of gender-based violence who want to speak out against abuse: the legal teams of powerful men who suppress allegations and prevent newspapers from running stories. Join renowned human rights lawyers and co-authors, Jennifer Robinson and Keina Yoshida, for an intense discussion about the vital changes which can protect and advance the progress made so far. Chaired by Lucia Osborne-Crowley.

Title: Lessons in Love with Liv Little & Caleb Azumah Nelson
Teaser: With exhilarating honesty, these two novelists write about the concerns of their generation: love, friendship, identity, and minimum wage jobs. Liv Little, founder of gal-dem, makes her fiction debut with Rosewater, about Elsie who writes poetry between...
Description: With exhilarating honesty, these two novelists write about the concerns of their generation: love, friendship, identity, and minimum wage jobs. Liv Little, founder of gal-dem, makes her fiction debut with Rosewater, about Elsie who writes poetry between shifts at her local gay bar; and Caleb Azumah Nelson, the Costa Book Award winner for Open Water, returns to the Festival with Small Worlds, following Stephen, searching for himself in London and Ghana. In conversation with Lil Green.

Title: Sue Hendra and Paul Linnet: Supertato - The Origin
Teaser: Ever wondered how Supertato got his superpowers? Supertato: Mean Green Time Machine is the latest ‘peel good’ story from dynamic duo, Sue Hendra and Paul Linnet. Charge your flux capacitors and travel back in time to discover your beloved...
Description: Ever wondered how Supertato got his superpowers? Supertato: Mean Green Time Machine is the latest ‘peel good’ story from dynamic duo, Sue Hendra and Paul Linnet. Charge your flux capacitors and travel back in time to discover your beloved supermarket superhero’s origin story! Packed with stories, songs, and silliness, this event will definitely count as one of your five a day!

Title: Leah Broad: Singing Women’s Praises
Teaser: Classical music has long been a male-dominated affair. Historical musicologist Leah Broad is determined to redress the balance and in Quartet: How Four Women Changed the Musical World she chronicles the lives and work of 20th century composers, Ethel...
Description: Classical music has long been a male-dominated affair. Historical musicologist Leah Broad is determined to redress the balance and in Quartet: How Four Women Changed the Musical World she chronicles the lives and work of 20th century composers, Ethel Smyth, Rebecca Clarke, Dorothy Howell, and Doreen Carwithen. Today at the Book Festival, Broad shares her project and her illuminating book.

Title: Kathryn Scanlan: Behind the Stable Door
Teaser: An extraordinary achievement of memoir and form, Kick the Latch was written by Kathryn Scanlan after hours of interviews with Sonia, a horse trainer working at a Midwest horse track. The brutality and beauty of Sonia’s life on the track is told in...
Description: An extraordinary achievement of memoir and form, Kick the Latch was written by Kathryn Scanlan after hours of interviews with Sonia, a horse trainer working at a Midwest horse track. The brutality and beauty of Sonia’s life on the track is told in minimalist, artful, and occasionally shocking vignettes. Join Scanlan as she discusses turning real life into a thrilling narrative ride with Rebecca Tamás.

Title: Two Beano Editors Make Mega Mischief
Teaser: Come and join the mischief in this interactive session with two Beano comic Editors, Craig Graham and Mike Stirling. Together they’re in charge of making sure that everything in Beano is as funny and naughty as it can possibly be! Mike and Craig...
Description: Come and join the mischief in this interactive session with two Beano comic Editors, Craig Graham and Mike Stirling. Together they’re in charge of making sure that everything in Beano is as funny and naughty as it can possibly be! Mike and Craig will reveal their top tips for creating laugh out loud stories, share jokes from their latest Boomic, Little Menace’s Great Escape, and take you on a behind-the-scenes tour of Beanotown’s greatest secrets as the comic celebrates its 85th birthday this year.

Title: Deborah Levy: Reflections On Identity
Teaser: Following the completion of her trilogy of formally inventive ‘living autobiographies’, Deborah Levy is widely regarded as one of the great writers of her generation. She returns to Edinburgh to discuss August Blue, an exceptional novel of fractured...
Description: Following the completion of her trilogy of formally inventive ‘living autobiographies’, Deborah Levy is widely regarded as one of the great writers of her generation. She returns to Edinburgh to discuss August Blue, an exceptional novel of fractured identity, written in her typically alluring style. Today Levy enters into dialogue about this mesmerising portrait of a piano virtuoso with Guardian chief culture writer Charlotte Higgins.

Title: Goddesses and Heroines with Jean Menzies
Teaser: Discover stories of mythical women from across the world with ancient historian and award-winning author Jean Menzies. Find out how Japanese goddess of the dawn Ame-no-Uzume saved the day by dancing; how the Ancient Greek witch Medea defeated a dragon;...
Description: Discover stories of mythical women from across the world with ancient historian and award-winning author Jean Menzies. Find out how Japanese goddess of the dawn Ame-no-Uzume saved the day by dancing; how the Ancient Greek witch Medea defeated a dragon; and how an ordinary woman outsmarted the tricky Scottish fairy Whuppity Stoorie, as Jean shares her new collection, Goddesses and Heroines.

Title: Families, Memories, and Stories with Katya Balen and Nadine Aisha Jassat
Teaser: Katya Balen and Nadine Aisha Jassat are two award-winning authors who will be sharing their storytelling process and introducing their extraordinary new books, The Light in Everything and The Stories Grandma Forgot (and How I Found Them). Both...
Description: Katya Balen and Nadine Aisha Jassat are two award-winning authors who will be sharing their storytelling process and introducing their extraordinary new books, The Light in Everything and The Stories Grandma Forgot (and How I Found Them). Both absolutely gripping, they tell two beautiful tales rooted in the importance of family, memories, and diving into the unknown with hope in your heart. Chaired by Patrice Lawrence.

Title: André Dao: Inheriting the Past
Teaser: Melbourne-based writer, artist, and activist, André Dao discusses his anticipated debut novel, Anam, featuring a narrator haunted by his grandfather’s ten-year imprisonment by the Communist government in Vietnam’s notorious Chi Hoa prison. In a...
Description: Melbourne-based writer, artist, and activist, André Dao discusses his anticipated debut novel, Anam, featuring a narrator haunted by his grandfather’s ten-year imprisonment by the Communist government in Vietnam’s notorious Chi Hoa prison. In a globe-spanning story following an endless series of wars and displacements, Anam blends fiction, essay, and theory to imagine history which has been repressed and forgotten by archives and by families. In conversation with Andrés N Ordorica.

Title: Go on a Lifesize Animal Adventure with Sophy Henn
Teaser: Sophy Henn's exciting new book, Lifesize Deadly Animals is the perfect introduction to animals for children, and this exciting event is packed full of animal facts as well as some deadly drawing fun! Watch out for the LIFESIZE black caiman jaws, Burmese...
Description: Sophy Henn's exciting new book, Lifesize Deadly Animals is the perfect introduction to animals for children, and this exciting event is packed full of animal facts as well as some deadly drawing fun! Watch out for the LIFESIZE black caiman jaws, Burmese python, slow loris and much more!

Title: Samanta Schweblin & Fernanda Trías: Strangely Familiar
Teaser: First published in Argentina in 2015 and now finally available in English, Fernanda Trías’s Pink Slime traces the complications of re-imagining family in the wake of ecological disaster while Samanta Schweblin’s short stories, Seven Empty Houses,...
Description: First published in Argentina in 2015 and now finally available in English, Fernanda Trías’s Pink Slime traces the complications of re-imagining family in the wake of ecological disaster while Samanta Schweblin’s short stories, Seven Empty Houses, sets the comforts of home off-kilter. Trías and Schweblin join us to discuss the complexity of finding where home lies in a turbulent world and the islands of respite that make life worth living. Chaired by Heather Parry.

Title: Octavia Bright: A Place of Care
Teaser: Spanning seven years, Octavia Bright’s debut memoir intertwines the author’s recovery from alcohol addiction with her father’s descent into Alzheimer’s. The parallel journeys of This Ragged Grace offer illuminating and generous reckonings with...
Description: Spanning seven years, Octavia Bright’s debut memoir intertwines the author’s recovery from alcohol addiction with her father’s descent into Alzheimer’s. The parallel journeys of This Ragged Grace offer illuminating and generous reckonings with recovery and grief. Join Bright, co-host of the Literary Friction podcast, for a wide-ranging discussion on art, family, and loss with Lucia Osborne-Crowley.

Title: Stomp! Stomp! Stomp! With Alastair Chisholm and Alex Willmore
Teaser: Join dynamic duo Alastair Chisholm and Alex Willmore for an interactive storytelling adventure with One Hungry Dragon's, Bernardo. A laugh-out-loud picture book event with a counting theme, a creative draw along, and one very big BURP that's guaranteed...
Description: Join dynamic duo Alastair Chisholm and Alex Willmore for an interactive storytelling adventure with One Hungry Dragon's, Bernardo. A laugh-out-loud picture book event with a counting theme, a creative draw along, and one very big BURP that's guaranteed to get children giggling.

Title: Nazneen Ahmed Pathak & S F Said: Into the Unknown Wonders of London
Teaser: In every city around the world, magic sleeps under streets, behind locked doors, and beneath piles of ordinary rubbish. Anything sleeping, however, must eventually awake. Join the authors of acclaimed new books City of Stolen Magic and Tyger, Nazneen...
Description: In every city around the world, magic sleeps under streets, behind locked doors, and beneath piles of ordinary rubbish. Anything sleeping, however, must eventually awake. Join the authors of acclaimed new books City of Stolen Magic and Tyger, Nazneen Ahmed Pathak and S F Said, for a discussion about the power of children's literature to stir the sorcery in your life. Joined in conversation by Melanie Ramdarshan Bold.

Title: Hannah Gold: Animal Friendships
Teaser: Join bestselling author, Hannah Gold, and take a deep dive into The Lost Whale, a beautiful story about hope, healing, and the incredible bond between children and animals. Hannah will also share an exclusive reading of Finding Bear, the...
Description: Join bestselling author, Hannah Gold, and take a deep dive into The Lost Whale, a beautiful story about hope, healing, and the incredible bond between children and animals. Hannah will also share an exclusive reading of Finding Bear, the much-anticipated sequel to The Last Bear – winner of last year's Waterstones and Blue Peter Book Awards. PLUS be in with a chance of winning an early draft copy before it hits the shelves!

Title: Spectacular Scottish Women with Louise Baillie, Eilidh Muldoon & Rose Reilly
Teaser: Discover the women who have shaped and shaken up Scotland in this fascinating, celebratory event with author Louise Baillie and illustrator Eilidh Muldoon, creators of Spectacular Scottish Women. From Paralympians to queens, activists to engineers,...
Description: Discover the women who have shaped and shaken up Scotland in this fascinating, celebratory event with author Louise Baillie and illustrator Eilidh Muldoon, creators of Spectacular Scottish Women. From Paralympians to queens, activists to engineers, Louise and Eilidh highlight the amazing lives of Scottish women. Hear their stories, discover how Eilidh brought them to life in her signature beautiful and bold illustration style, and meet international footballer Rose Reilly, who inspired the book!

Title: Joseph Coelho and Fiona Lumbers: Hooked on Books
Teaser: Waterstones Children's Laureate Joseph Coelho and illustrator Fiona Lumbers present the latest instalment of their much-loved picture book series, Luna Loves Books. On the biggest, bookiest day of the year, Luna’s class is celebrating books. Everyone...
Description: Waterstones Children's Laureate Joseph Coelho and illustrator Fiona Lumbers present the latest instalment of their much-loved picture book series, Luna Loves Books. On the biggest, bookiest day of the year, Luna’s class is celebrating books. Everyone is dressed up, but disaster strikes as her costume rips. Can Luna’s dad come to the rescue with book magic? With interactive songs, live drawing, and readings, this is a family show not to be missed!

Title: Oliver Mol: Train Lord
Teaser: When he was 25, critically acclaimed writer Oliver Mol’s life was derailed by a 10-month migraine. Unable to write and barely able to look at screens, Mol took a job as a train guard in Sydney. This inspired Train Lord: a sensitive and tentative...
Description: When he was 25, critically acclaimed writer Oliver Mol’s life was derailed by a 10-month migraine. Unable to write and barely able to look at screens, Mol took a job as a train guard in Sydney. This inspired Train Lord: a sensitive and tentative rebuilding of his sense of self. He has since turned his story into an award-winning performance. Join Mol as he brings his fragmentary and powerful memoir to life. In conversation with Dan Richards.

Title: Rachel Connolly & Michael Magee: Near and Far
Teaser: In their electrifying debut novels, Rachel Connolly and Michael Magee grapple with friendship and uncertain futures that come with being young and being home against the backdrop of Belfast. Magee’s Close To Home draws on his own experiences to...
Description: In their electrifying debut novels, Rachel Connolly and Michael Magee grapple with friendship and uncertain futures that come with being young and being home against the backdrop of Belfast. Magee’s Close To Home draws on his own experiences to question the forces shaping modern masculinity, while Connolly’s Lazy City is about love, grief, and finding yourself where you are. Chaired by Caoilinn Hughes.

Title: Frances Hardinge: Unravelling Stories
Teaser: No one twists a tale like Frances Hardinge. Her latest book, Unraveller, is a deliciously dark fairytale about trauma and recovery, and rage and redemption. In a world where anyone can create a life-destroying curse, only one person has the power to...
Description: No one twists a tale like Frances Hardinge. Her latest book, Unraveller, is a deliciously dark fairytale about trauma and recovery, and rage and redemption. In a world where anyone can create a life-destroying curse, only one person has the power to unravel them. This event lets you peek inside Frances’ imagination and discover how she creates the dark, quirky and fantastical worlds of her stories. Chaired by Nadine Aisha Jassat.

Title: Tessa Hadley: Everyday Turmoil
Teaser: The lauded novelist of Free Love and Late in the Day returns to the Festival to discuss her latest collection, After the Funeral. These dazzling stories demonstrate Hadley’s skill at depicting and excoriating the travails of everyday life, where...
Description: The lauded novelist of Free Love and Late in the Day returns to the Festival to discuss her latest collection, After the Funeral. These dazzling stories demonstrate Hadley’s skill at depicting and excoriating the travails of everyday life, where seemingly insignificant moments result in major consequences, while fleetingly laying bare the underlying conflicts that govern our lives and relationships. In conversation with Lennie Goodings.

Title: Jacqueline Rose: The Empathy Epidemic
Teaser: Amid the harrowing losses of the Covid-19 pandemic, there was also the potential for radical empathy wrought by shared experience. Jacqueline Rose’s The Plague takes the pandemic as a starting point to unravel recent history via the lives and works...
Description: Amid the harrowing losses of the Covid-19 pandemic, there was also the potential for radical empathy wrought by shared experience. Jacqueline Rose’s The Plague takes the pandemic as a starting point to unravel recent history via the lives and works of three extraordinary thinkers, Albert Camus, Sigmund Freud, and Simone Weil. Join Rose and Charlotte Higgins for an emotive and enlightening discussion.

Title: Maz Evans: Myths and Mayhem
Teaser: Get ready for an Ancient Greek adventure that’s out of this Underworld! Maz Evans is the multi award-winning author of the internationally bestselling series, Who Let the Gods Out? Be prepared to laugh your sandals off as Maz leads an anarchic hour of...
Description: Get ready for an Ancient Greek adventure that’s out of this Underworld! Maz Evans is the multi award-winning author of the internationally bestselling series, Who Let the Gods Out? Be prepared to laugh your sandals off as Maz leads an anarchic hour of fun and games as she introduces you to a gang of misfit immortals. It’s Greek mythology, but not as you know it!

Title: Sebastian Barry & Steven Isserlis: Things We Don’t Remember and Things We Can’t Forget
Teaser: What is Old God’s Time? It’s ancient history and it’s an almost impossibly moving, unforgettable story from one of Ireland’s greatest living authors. This novel – surely Sebastian Barry’s masterpiece – is set by the seaside near Dublin,...
Description: What is Old God’s Time? It’s ancient history and it’s an almost impossibly moving, unforgettable story from one of Ireland’s greatest living authors. This novel – surely Sebastian Barry’s masterpiece – is set by the seaside near Dublin, where old Tom Kettle is musing over a lifetime of vivid memories. Join Barry in lively discussion with Nick Barley, where he will also give a reading with musical accompaniment by renowned cellist Steven Isserlis.

Title: Jacqueline Crooks & Yara Rodrigues Fowler: Current Affairs
Teaser: In Jacqueline Crooks’ debut novel Fire Rush, a young woman enters an intoxicating world of dancehall and gangsters in 1970s west London. Yara Rodrigues Fowler’s There are More Things chronicles the political turbulence of 2016 in Brazil and the UK...
Description: In Jacqueline Crooks’ debut novel Fire Rush, a young woman enters an intoxicating world of dancehall and gangsters in 1970s west London. Yara Rodrigues Fowler’s There are More Things chronicles the political turbulence of 2016 in Brazil and the UK through the eyes of two women. Join a conversation about intertwining real politics and history with fictional characters who find strength despite their circumstances. Chaired by Tomiwa Folorunso.

Title: Julia Donaldson and Friends: The Amazing World of Julia Donaldson
Teaser: Join the UK’s bestselling author, Julia Donaldson, for a fun-packed hour of rip-roaring songs, storytelling, and much more. Julia Donaldson will perform stories including The Gruffalo and her latest hit The Bowerbird. There will also be a special...
Description: Join the UK’s bestselling author, Julia Donaldson, for a fun-packed hour of rip-roaring songs, storytelling, and much more. Julia Donaldson will perform stories including The Gruffalo and her latest hit The Bowerbird. There will also be a special appearance from Lydia Monks, illustrator of the bestselling What the Ladybird Heard series and Sugarlump and the Unicorn.

Title: Tyrolean Tales with Jon Klassen
Teaser: Jon Klassen’s striking illustrations and minimalist text have made his work modern classics and won him a legion of fans, both young and old, not to mention many awards. This characteristic style follows him in his gloriously gothic new book, The...
Description: Jon Klassen’s striking illustrations and minimalist text have made his work modern classics and won him a legion of fans, both young and old, not to mention many awards. This characteristic style follows him in his gloriously gothic new book, The Skull: his first for middle-grade readers. Meet Jon and discover how he created his captivating, monochrome illustrations in this eerie, enchanting event.

Title: Lizzie Huxley-Jones, Ross Montgomery & E L Norry: Magical Destinies
Teaser: Have you ever felt certain that you’re destined for greatness? Arthurian legend is brought into the modern world in three new edge-of-your-seat fantasy adventures: Lizzie Huxley-Jones’s Vivi Conway and the Sword of Legend, E L Norry’s Fablehouse,...
Description: Have you ever felt certain that you’re destined for greatness? Arthurian legend is brought into the modern world in three new edge-of-your-seat fantasy adventures: Lizzie Huxley-Jones’s Vivi Conway and the Sword of Legend, E L Norry’s Fablehouse, and Ross Montgomery’s Spellstone. Discover the inspiration for their books in an event packed with magic and monsters, swords and sorcerers, and friends and fiends. Your destiny awaits… Chaired by Vivian French.

Title: Max Porter: Boyhood
Teaser: ‘I loved Shy. I finished it elated and tearful[…] changed by the journey.’ So said P J Harvey of Max Porter’s latest novel, widely considered a masterpiece. Fans of Lanny will be entranced by this deeply tender and humane portrait of a troubled...
Description: ‘I loved Shy. I finished it elated and tearful[…] changed by the journey.’ So said P J Harvey of Max Porter’s latest novel, widely considered a masterpiece. Fans of Lanny will be entranced by this deeply tender and humane portrait of a troubled teenager. This special event includes a unique performance of Shy with Porter alongside the Citizens Theatre’s WAC Ensemble – Scotland’s first theatre company for theatremakers with care experience.

Title: The World of Japanese Spirits with Chie Kutsuwada & Julian Sedgwick
Teaser: Dare you enter the haunted heart of Japan? Author and illustrator duo, Julian Sedgwick and Chie Kutsuwada – creators of Tsunami Girl – invite you into the fascinating world of Japanese ghosts and spirituality. Learn about mythical yōkai and...
Description: Dare you enter the haunted heart of Japan? Author and illustrator duo, Julian Sedgwick and Chie Kutsuwada – creators of Tsunami Girl – invite you into the fascinating world of Japanese ghosts and spirituality. Learn about mythical yōkai and tsukumogami, from their traditional roots to the modern day, and find out why, even now, incredible worlds exist just beyond the visible. Then watch Chie conjure a manga yōkai as Julian reads an exclusive preview from 100 Tales from the Tokyo Ghost Café.

Title: Jeremy Deller: It's Time to Lose Control
Teaser: Whether it’s a filmed re-enactment of the Battle of Orgreave, when miners and police came into conflict during the 1984 strike, or a free bouncy castle in the shape of Stonehenge sited on Glasgow Green, Jeremy Deller’s art projects open their arms...
Description: Whether it’s a filmed re-enactment of the Battle of Orgreave, when miners and police came into conflict during the 1984 strike, or a free bouncy castle in the shape of Stonehenge sited on Glasgow Green, Jeremy Deller’s art projects open their arms and welcome the public in. Join him in a wide-ranging discussion, on his new book Art Is Magic and more, with Guardian chief culture writer Charlotte Higgins.

Title: Michael Rosen: How We Recover
Teaser: The beloved former Children’s Laureate joins us to discuss his memoir Getting Better. Michael Rosen has encountered much tragedy and trauma in his life: the death of a child, debilitating chronic illness, and a near death experience from Covid-19....
Description: The beloved former Children’s Laureate joins us to discuss his memoir Getting Better. Michael Rosen has encountered much tragedy and trauma in his life: the death of a child, debilitating chronic illness, and a near death experience from Covid-19. This book, examining roads to recovery, is a typically generous exploration of how to live well again after, or during, our darkest moments. In conversation with Richard Holloway.

Title: Simon Schama: The Health of Nations
Teaser: With over 50 BBC documentaries to his name, Simon Schama is one of Britain’s best-known historians. Now he’s looking at how we respond to plagues and pandemics. In Foreign Bodies, Schama recounts gripping stories of smallpox in London, cholera in...
Description: With over 50 BBC documentaries to his name, Simon Schama is one of Britain’s best-known historians. Now he’s looking at how we respond to plagues and pandemics. In Foreign Bodies, Schama recounts gripping stories of smallpox in London, cholera in Paris, and plague in India threaded together by the story of the man who developed the first mass-produced vaccine. This is a history of how humans have – so far – avoided extinction. In conversation with Allan Little.

Title: Sin Blaché & Helen Macdonald: Double Agents
Teaser: What if your happiest memories were turned against you? In the thrilling science fiction novel, Prophet, memories materialise as weapons and an unlikely pair of investigators must join forces to battle a strange new reality. Join writer and musician Sin...
Description: What if your happiest memories were turned against you? In the thrilling science fiction novel, Prophet, memories materialise as weapons and an unlikely pair of investigators must join forces to battle a strange new reality. Join writer and musician Sin Blaché and their co-author, H is For Hawk writer Helen Macdonald to discuss their inventive new novel, dynamic duos, and the weaponisation of nostalgia. Chaired by Mary Paulson-Ellis.

Title: David Greig & Alan Warner: Scottish Legends Retold
Teaser: Brace yourself for exhilarating versions of two classic Scottish stories. Columba’s Bones is the debut novel from playwright David Greig, which reimagines 9th century Iona as the setting for a ‘heist gone wrong’. Alan Warner’s Nothing Left to...
Description: Brace yourself for exhilarating versions of two classic Scottish stories. Columba’s Bones is the debut novel from playwright David Greig, which reimagines 9th century Iona as the setting for a ‘heist gone wrong’. Alan Warner’s Nothing Left to Fear From Hell reimagines the aftermath of Culloden, when Bonnie Prince Charlie flees into the Highlands. Join Sally Magnusson as she speaks with Greig and Warner in this unmissable event about our history.

Title: Charms and Curses with Elle McNicoll
Teaser: In Like a Curse, the fantastic sequel, to Like a Charm, festival favourite Elle McNicoll takes us to her hometown of Edinburgh, but not as we know it. This thrilling and heart-warming conclusion to her enthralling fantasy duology sees our witch heroine...
Description: In Like a Curse, the fantastic sequel, to Like a Charm, festival favourite Elle McNicoll takes us to her hometown of Edinburgh, but not as we know it. This thrilling and heart-warming conclusion to her enthralling fantasy duology sees our witch heroine Ramya battle Sirens to save her family, friends, and the unsuspecting citizens of Edinburgh. Join Elle to discover how she combines the real and mystical in her fantastic series, and why she chose to have a neurodivergent young witch as her main character. Chaired by Nazneen Ahmed Pathak

Title: Introducing The Star Whale with Nicola Davies and Petr Horáček
Teaser: Join internationally acclaimed duo Nicola Davies and Petr Horáček for a unique celebration of our beautiful planet, in verse and live drawing. Discover a pangolin at dusk, fly on a bat’s back, visit a lion, and hear about his plight! You might even...
Description: Join internationally acclaimed duo Nicola Davies and Petr Horáček for a unique celebration of our beautiful planet, in verse and live drawing. Discover a pangolin at dusk, fly on a bat’s back, visit a lion, and hear about his plight! You might even spot a kingfisher, that ‘small glint of wonder’, and see how ‘wild reclaims the world’ in the urban night-time!

Title: Jasmine Donahaye & Frieda Hughes: The Language of Birds
Teaser: Two incredible writers help us explore new ways of seeing the natural world. Jasmine Donahaye’s Birdsplaining: A Natural History explains how a wren in the house foretells a death, while crows’ misbehaviour suggests how the ‘natural’ order may...
Description: Two incredible writers help us explore new ways of seeing the natural world. Jasmine Donahaye’s Birdsplaining: A Natural History explains how a wren in the house foretells a death, while crows’ misbehaviour suggests how the ‘natural’ order may be challenged. Poet and painter Frieda Hughes writes a story of love, obsession, and nature as she rescues a chick in George: A Magpie Memoir. Chaired by Amanda Thomson.

Title: Dr Sheila Kanani: 'Houston, We Have a Rainbow!'
Teaser: Why is blood red? Why are carrots orange? Is the sky really blue? Real life astronomer, Dr Sheila Kanani, answers these questions and many more in her latest book, Can You Get Rainbows in Space? Let your curiosity play amongst the stars as Dr Sheila...
Description: Why is blood red? Why are carrots orange? Is the sky really blue? Real life astronomer, Dr Sheila Kanani, answers these questions and many more in her latest book, Can You Get Rainbows in Space? Let your curiosity play amongst the stars as Dr Sheila leads this interactive event full of spectacular experiments and even shows you how to make a space rainbow!

Title: Jolyon Maugham KC: Fight the Power. Keep the Receipts
Teaser: As founder of the Good Law Project, Jolyon Maugham KC is known for holding public bodies and government to account. Challenging the prorogation of parliament during the Brexit negotiations, investigating alleged cronyism in the awarding of PPE...
Description: As founder of the Good Law Project, Jolyon Maugham KC is known for holding public bodies and government to account. Challenging the prorogation of parliament during the Brexit negotiations, investigating alleged cronyism in the awarding of PPE contracts; Maugham joins us with his book Bringing Down Goliath, a convincing case for how the law can be a force for social change.

Title: Kiran Millwood Hargrave & Katherine Rundell: Power, Knowledge and Love
Teaser: There’s a place where all the wildest stories began. From these award-winning queens of fiction comes two new stories of power, knowledge, and love. In the Shadow of the Wolf Queen and Impossible Creatures mark the start of two epic new fantasy...
Description: There’s a place where all the wildest stories began. From these award-winning queens of fiction comes two new stories of power, knowledge, and love. In the Shadow of the Wolf Queen and Impossible Creatures mark the start of two epic new fantasy trilogies. Join Kiran Millwood Hargrave and Katherine Rundell for a discussion on building their magical worlds and creating the characters and creatures that inhabit them. Chaired by Hannah Lavery.

Title: Kübra Gümüşy, R F Kuang & Irene Vallejo: A Short History of Language
Teaser: Three lauded authors discuss how the past, present, and future of language is explored in their respective books. Irene Vallejo’s Papyrus, is a bestselling history of books and libraries in the ancient world; R F Kuang’s historical novel Babel is...
Description: Three lauded authors discuss how the past, present, and future of language is explored in their respective books. Irene Vallejo’s Papyrus, is a bestselling history of books and libraries in the ancient world; R F Kuang’s historical novel Babel is set in the Oxford Royal Institute of Translation; and Kübra Gümüşy’s Speaking and Being is an exploration of how language can shape our thinking and determine our politics. Chaired by Daniel Hahn.

Title: Lex Croucher & Cynthia So: Queer in Love
Teaser: Join leading YA authors Lex Croucher and Cynthia So in discussing the versatile ways of writing about queer love. In Gwen and Art Are Not in Love, Lex plunges into a medieval period drama that will have you cry-laughing. In If You Still Recognise Me,...
Description: Join leading YA authors Lex Croucher and Cynthia So in discussing the versatile ways of writing about queer love. In Gwen and Art Are Not in Love, Lex plunges into a medieval period drama that will have you cry-laughing. In If You Still Recognise Me, Cynthia explores the emotional ups and downs of a long-distance relationship. In both, the rewards will be worth the heartache and lives will be changed forever. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

Title: Angela Saini: How Men Came to Rule
Teaser: How did we end up with a system that prioritises for one gender over any other? In her bold and optimistic study of the patriarchy, Angela Saini uncovers a complex history of male domination. Just as gender roles and assumptions have changed, 'the fight...
Description: How did we end up with a system that prioritises for one gender over any other? In her bold and optimistic study of the patriarchy, Angela Saini uncovers a complex history of male domination. Just as gender roles and assumptions have changed, 'the fight for a fairer and more equal society is constantly repositioning itself too.' Join Saini for an illuminating discussion with Roxani Krystalli about how we can live differently.

Title: Constance Debré: Defiance and Freedom
Teaser: Judgements over what a mother is and isn’t allowed to do never seem to end. When Constance Debré is separated from her young child after telling her ex-husband that she is dating women, she fears a monastic and loveless existence. Instead, she lives...
Description: Judgements over what a mother is and isn’t allowed to do never seem to end. When Constance Debré is separated from her young child after telling her ex-husband that she is dating women, she fears a monastic and loveless existence. Instead, she lives for herself. Stark, beautiful and humane, Love Me Tender is a bold account of the impossible sacrifices asked of mothers, and shows us that there are many ways to live well. In conversation with Kirsty Logan.

Title: Pamela Butchart: A Treasure Trove of Trouble
Teaser: Izzy and her friends are back for more classroom chaos in Blue Peter Book Award-winner Pamela Butchart’s latest book, There’s a Beast in the Basement! This time Izzy is on the hunt for treasure buried beneath Wigglesbottom Primary. But the teachers...
Description: Izzy and her friends are back for more classroom chaos in Blue Peter Book Award-winner Pamela Butchart’s latest book, There’s a Beast in the Basement! This time Izzy is on the hunt for treasure buried beneath Wigglesbottom Primary. But the teachers aren’t the only beastly beings inhabiting the halls… Be prepared to laugh your gym pants off as Pamela shares her hilarious stories in this fun-filled interactive event.

Title: R F Kuang: Someone Else's Story
Teaser: After the stratospheric success of her dark academic fantasy novel Babel, R F Kuang has elegantly pivoted genre to literary thriller. June, an aspiring author, steals her dead friend’s manuscript and publishes it to rave acclaim. When threatened with...
Description: After the stratospheric success of her dark academic fantasy novel Babel, R F Kuang has elegantly pivoted genre to literary thriller. June, an aspiring author, steals her dead friend’s manuscript and publishes it to rave acclaim. When threatened with exposure, June will go to any length to keep her secret. Join the New York Times bestselling author as she discusses Yellowface, a rollicking satire that skewers the publishing industry, Twitter discourse, and co opted identity politics. In conversation with Nyla Ahmad.

Title: Paul Murray: Painfully Funny Fiction
Teaser: The word ‘tragicomic’ could have been invented for Irish author Paul Murray, who hit the bullseye a decade ago with his simultaneously hilarious and devastating novel, Skippy Dies. Now he may even have surpassed that success with his fourth novel,...
Description: The word ‘tragicomic’ could have been invented for Irish author Paul Murray, who hit the bullseye a decade ago with his simultaneously hilarious and devastating novel, Skippy Dies. Now he may even have surpassed that success with his fourth novel, The Bee Sting, in which one unlucky moment is the trigger for a sequence of unfortunate events. Join Murray for an hour of savage humour and poetic insights. In conversation with Peggy Hughes.

Title: L R Lam: World Building and Dividing
Teaser: From epic fantasy romance to space opera, near-future cyberpunk to a magical circus: L R Lam is not afraid to explore new worlds. In today's event hear about Lam’s new epic fantasy trilogy which launches with Dragonfall where, long ago, humans...
Description: From epic fantasy romance to space opera, near-future cyberpunk to a magical circus: L R Lam is not afraid to explore new worlds. In today's event hear about Lam’s new epic fantasy trilogy which launches with Dragonfall where, long ago, humans betrayed dragons, stealing their magic and banishing them to a dying world. Centuries later, their descendants worship dragons as gods. But the gods remember, and they do not forgive. Chaired by Alice Tarbuck.

Title: Mary Jean Chan & Nina Mingya Powles: New Poems
Teaser: These two poets dwell in the ever-shifting textures of language. Mary Jean Chan follows up their award-winning debut Flèche with Bright Fear, a radiant collection that reckons with queerphobia and anti-Asian racism and finds refuge in the radical power...
Description: These two poets dwell in the ever-shifting textures of language. Mary Jean Chan follows up their award-winning debut Flèche with Bright Fear, a radiant collection that reckons with queerphobia and anti-Asian racism and finds refuge in the radical power of poetry. Joining Chan is poet and essayist Nina Mingya Powles, whose first collection, Magnolia, finds joy in multiplicities: of identities, sensations, and inheritances. Please note, Mary Jean Chan will appear remotely. Chaired by Alycia Pirmohamed.

Title: Sally Huband & Malachy Tallack: The Shape of Water
Teaser: Join the writers of two moving nature memoirs which explore the ongoing allure of the water. Malachy Tallack’s Illuminated by Water uses his decades long passion for fly fishing to explore ‘wildness’, and how we use that concept to engage with...
Description: Join the writers of two moving nature memoirs which explore the ongoing allure of the water. Malachy Tallack’s Illuminated by Water uses his decades long passion for fly fishing to explore ‘wildness’, and how we use that concept to engage with nature; while Sally Huband’s Sea Bean is a moving story of beachcombing for the titular bean, a seed with mystical significance. Chaired by Dan Richards.

Title: James Kelman: Class Act
Teaser: It’s impossible to overstate the importance of James Kelman and his landmark 1994 Booker Prize win for Scottish literature. Nearly 30 years on, we welcome Kelman back to the Festival to speak with writer Graeme Armstrong on God's Teeth and Other...
Description: It’s impossible to overstate the importance of James Kelman and his landmark 1994 Booker Prize win for Scottish literature. Nearly 30 years on, we welcome Kelman back to the Festival to speak with writer Graeme Armstrong on God's Teeth and Other Phenomena, a classic example of his observant and eviscerating style.

Title: Kim Sherwood: Women in Writing
Teaser: Kim Sherwood was described by Hilary Mantel as 'a writer of capacity, potency and sophistication'. A Wild & True Relation, is a remake of the 18th century heroic novel. Molly, an orphan on board a ship who's disguised as a boy, grows up to outshine the...
Description: Kim Sherwood was described by Hilary Mantel as 'a writer of capacity, potency and sophistication'. A Wild & True Relation, is a remake of the 18th century heroic novel. Molly, an orphan on board a ship who's disguised as a boy, grows up to outshine the men around her and create her own legacy. Join Sherwood for this celebration of women in writing and women's roles throughout history. In conversation with Jenny Brown.

Title: Tania Branigan: History - Adjust as Necessary
Teaser: China’s Cultural Revolution ended 50 years ago, but its scar runs through the heart of Chinese society. As the Guardian’s foreign leader writer, Tania Branigan spent seven years there, and Red Memory is the result: a courageous analysis of the past...
Description: China’s Cultural Revolution ended 50 years ago, but its scar runs through the heart of Chinese society. As the Guardian’s foreign leader writer, Tania Branigan spent seven years there, and Red Memory is the result: a courageous analysis of the past that haunts China today. At a time of fear mongering and top-down manipulation of public sentiment in the West, Branigan’s account may also have resonances closer to home. In conversation with Jenny Niven.

Title: A N Wilson: Coming to Terms
Teaser: A N Wilson was at the first Edinburgh International Book Festival 40 years ago. Since then, he has produced millions of words of journalism, 20 novels and a barrage of biographies. Yet somehow he looks back and sees ‘a life of failed promises’....
Description: A N Wilson was at the first Edinburgh International Book Festival 40 years ago. Since then, he has produced millions of words of journalism, 20 novels and a barrage of biographies. Yet somehow he looks back and sees ‘a life of failed promises’. Confessions is a memoir of Wilson’s early life: an exercise in humility. Is he right to frame his unusually successful life in words of self-doubt? Join him in this lively conversation with Stuart Kelly.

Title: Ambrose Parry: The Thrill of the Unexplained
Teaser: Since Chris Brookmyre and Marisa Haetzman embarked on their journey as crime-writing duo Ambrose Parry, they’ve produced a series of tales in Victorian Edinburgh's underworld. In Voices of the Dead, Dr Will Raven and Sarah Fisher’s latest adventure,...
Description: Since Chris Brookmyre and Marisa Haetzman embarked on their journey as crime-writing duo Ambrose Parry, they’ve produced a series of tales in Victorian Edinburgh's underworld. In Voices of the Dead, Dr Will Raven and Sarah Fisher’s latest adventure, it’s 1853 and body parts have been found at Surgeon’s Hall – but they are not anatomy specimens. Immerse yourself in the mesmerising atmosphere of Auld Reekie in this unmissable session, chaired by Mary Paulson-Ellis.

Title: Sally Magnusson: What the Clearances Couldn’t Remove
Teaser: Although she’s best known as a BBC newsreader and her father was a famous Icelander, Sally Magnusson is descended on her mother’s side from victims of the Highland Clearances. That terrible period of Scottish history is at the heart of Magnusson’s...
Description: Although she’s best known as a BBC newsreader and her father was a famous Icelander, Sally Magnusson is descended on her mother’s side from victims of the Highland Clearances. That terrible period of Scottish history is at the heart of Magnusson’s new novel, Music in the Dark. Shot through with spirited resilience, it’s a tender, clear-eyed reckoning with Scotland’s past. In conversation with Graeme Macrae Burnet.

Title: V E Schwab: New Shades of Magic
Teaser: Join the international sensation and highly prolific V E Schwab as she discusses the death-defying fantasy The Invisible life of Addie Larue and launches a new trilogy in the Shades of Magic universe with The Fragile Threads of Power, which involves a...
Description: Join the international sensation and highly prolific V E Schwab as she discusses the death-defying fantasy The Invisible life of Addie Larue and launches a new trilogy in the Shades of Magic universe with The Fragile Threads of Power, which involves a desperate hunt to find an artefact that may prevent devastating conflict. This event will delight Schwab fans, and provide a tantalising beginning for the uninitiated. In conversation with Harry Josephine Giles.

Title: James Naughtie: When Knowledge Could Be Deadly
Teaser: James Naughtie has witnessed much political skulduggery as a special correspondent for BBC News, and he’s put this knowledge to use in his gripping spy thriller series. Today, Naughtie introduces The Spy Across the Water: the third outing for the...
Description: James Naughtie has witnessed much political skulduggery as a special correspondent for BBC News, and he’s put this knowledge to use in his gripping spy thriller series. Today, Naughtie introduces The Spy Across the Water: the third outing for the Flemyng brothers, bound together through espionage and embroiled in the Cold War. Hear Naughtie discuss this fascinating brainteaser which spans the streets of Washington DC and the Scottish Highlands. In conversation with Ruth Wishart.

Title: Lucy Jones & Szilvia Molnar: Maternity and Metamorphosis
Teaser: Early parenthood is a time of bliss and bewilderment, terror, and wonder. Szilvia Molnar’s debut novel The Nursery is a visceral and revelatory portrait of a woman struggling with maternal fear and its looming madness. In Matrescence, journalist Lucy...
Description: Early parenthood is a time of bliss and bewilderment, terror, and wonder. Szilvia Molnar’s debut novel The Nursery is a visceral and revelatory portrait of a woman struggling with maternal fear and its looming madness. In Matrescence, journalist Lucy Jones shows how the changes in the maternal mind, brain, and body are far more profound and enduring than we have been led to believe. Chaired by Kirsty Logan.

Title: Josie Long: Love Language
Teaser: Stand-up comedian and writer Josie Long has been charming Edinburgh audiences since she won Best Newcomer at the Fringe in 2006. Now, she turns her talents to fiction, with short story collection, Because I Don’t Know What You Mean and What You...
Description: Stand-up comedian and writer Josie Long has been charming Edinburgh audiences since she won Best Newcomer at the Fringe in 2006. Now, she turns her talents to fiction, with short story collection, Because I Don’t Know What You Mean and What You Don’t. Join us for an uplifting discussion on how storytelling and comedy can be an escape from the mayhem of modern life. In conversation with Viv Groskop.

Title: Hannah Lavery & Marjorie Lotfi: Being and Otherness
Teaser: Friends and creative collaborators, the poet and playwright Hannah Lavery and poet Marjorie Lotfi were awarded a Second Life grant from the Edwin Morgan Trust to respond to the poetry of Edwin Morgan while exploring their experience as 'mixed-race'...
Description: Friends and creative collaborators, the poet and playwright Hannah Lavery and poet Marjorie Lotfi were awarded a Second Life grant from the Edwin Morgan Trust to respond to the poetry of Edwin Morgan while exploring their experience as 'mixed-race' women in Scotland in poem-letters sent to one another across the spring of 2023. Join the supremely talented Lavery and Lotfi as they continue this excavation in this special performance and launch of their accompanying pamphlet.

Title: Rachelle Atalla & Ever Dundas: Tomorrow's Worlds
Teaser: Two thrillers take us to dystopian, and unnervingly feasible, futures. The world has run out of water in Rachelle Atalla’s novel Thirsty Animals in which a woman returns to her family home in the Scottish Borders and waits for the rain to come. In...
Description: Two thrillers take us to dystopian, and unnervingly feasible, futures. The world has run out of water in Rachelle Atalla’s novel Thirsty Animals in which a woman returns to her family home in the Scottish Borders and waits for the rain to come. In Ever Dundas’ novel, HellSans, a ubiquitous government-mandated typeface controls the UK population, while those allergic to the technology face persecution from society. Chaired by Eilidh Akilade.

Title: Peter Frankopan: Humanity and Climate Intertwined
Teaser: The Earth Transformed puts climate at the centre of world history. From the formation of Earth through the rise of human beings, Oxford historian Peter Frankopan demonstrates how climate shaped humanity and how it dominates politics, economics, and...
Description: The Earth Transformed puts climate at the centre of world history. From the formation of Earth through the rise of human beings, Oxford historian Peter Frankopan demonstrates how climate shaped humanity and how it dominates politics, economics, and society today. No stranger to intellectual adventures, Frankopan previously wrote The Silk Roads and The New Silk Roads: today he talks to Jo Sharp about his most ambitious project to date.

Title: Simon Sebag Montefiore: Family Matters
Teaser: Human beings have at least one thing in common: family. In his ambitious, scintillating, and epic work The World: A Family History, historian Simon Sebag Montefiore tells the story of humanity through the lens of dynasties; spanning centuries,...
Description: Human beings have at least one thing in common: family. In his ambitious, scintillating, and epic work The World: A Family History, historian Simon Sebag Montefiore tells the story of humanity through the lens of dynasties; spanning centuries, continents, and cultures. From the Medicis to the Mughals, and from the Assads to the Zulus, Montefiore presents a small selection of the families that have shaped our world. In conversation with Bidisha Mamata.

Title: Anna Funder: A Woman in Full
Teaser: Anna Funder has specialised in writing unconventional accounts of European history in her previous works Stasiland and All That I Am. Now, in Wifedom, she explores the unsung life of George Orwell’s brilliant wife, Eileen O’Shaughnessy. In this...
Description: Anna Funder has specialised in writing unconventional accounts of European history in her previous works Stasiland and All That I Am. Now, in Wifedom, she explores the unsung life of George Orwell’s brilliant wife, Eileen O’Shaughnessy. In this event, discover how Funder used newly-discovered letters to recreate the Orwells’ life during two major wars in Europe, and examine together what is the true price of women’s work.In conversation with Jenny Niven.

Title: Stories and Scran
Teaser: Returning for its fourth year, Stories and Scran celebrates the dynamic and thought-provoking work created by our Citizen participants. This year’s event showcases the diverse voices and creative talent from local groups across the city including the...
Description: Returning for its fourth year, Stories and Scran celebrates the dynamic and thought-provoking work created by our Citizen participants. This year’s event showcases the diverse voices and creative talent from local groups across the city including the Tollcross Writing Group, North Edinburgh Drama Group and WHALE Writers plus the Book Festival’s own Adult Writing Group and Citizen Collective. Find out more about our Communities Programme: ontheroad.edbookfest.co.uk

Title: Simone Seales: Sound Escapes
Teaser: Cellist, performer, and writer Simone Seales creates spaces of radical joy in classical music through their practice of improvisation and intersectional feminism. Today they join us for a special event – part musical performance, part spoken word –...
Description: Cellist, performer, and writer Simone Seales creates spaces of radical joy in classical music through their practice of improvisation and intersectional feminism. Today they join us for a special event – part musical performance, part spoken word – exploring the power of music and language to reflect and alter our emotional states of being.

Title: Katrín Jakobsdóttir & Ragnar Jónasson: Partners in Crime
Teaser: At the end of a long day, Iceland’s prime minister takes her mind off the pressures of leading a nation by writing Nordic noir. Already a scholar of crime fiction, Katrin Jakobsdóttir joined forces with bestselling crime writer Ragnar Jónasson to...

Title: Damian Barr Literary Salon
Teaser: Celebrated author, broadcaster, and host of The Big Scottish Book Club, Damian Barr is all about books - whether that’s through his own writing or by celebrating other people’s. We’re delighted to welcome him back to Edinburgh for an evening of...
Description: Celebrated author, broadcaster, and host of The Big Scottish Book Club, Damian Barr is all about books - whether that’s through his own writing or by celebrating other people’s. We’re delighted to welcome him back to Edinburgh for an evening of lively discussion, readings, and performance as we bring together some very special guests for this Edinburgh edition of his wildly popular Salon. Barr is joined by Monica Heisey, Hollie McNish and Michael Pedersen.

Title: Monica Heisey, Josie Long & Will McPhail: Funny Peculiar
Teaser: If you don’t laugh, you’ll cry – sometimes it’s better to do both. Schitt’s Creek writer Monica Heisey’s novel Really Good, Actually is one woman’s search for joy after divorce, while comedian Josie Long’s Because I Don’t Know What You...
Description: If you don’t laugh, you’ll cry – sometimes it’s better to do both. Schitt’s Creek writer Monica Heisey’s novel Really Good, Actually is one woman’s search for joy after divorce, while comedian Josie Long’s Because I Don’t Know What You Mean and What You Don’t explores love in the age of anxiety. They are joined by Will McPhail, whose Love & Vermin collects his distinctive and wise New Yorker cartoons. Chaired by Michael Williams.

Title: Letters of Hope
Teaser: What would you tell an outsider about where you live? What hopeful things would you write to your future self? These were two of the creative questions our writer in residence, Chris Barkley, has been exploring with young people from the Spartans...
Description: What would you tell an outsider about where you live? What hopeful things would you write to your future self? These were two of the creative questions our writer in residence, Chris Barkley, has been exploring with young people from the Spartans Alternative School. With short film, music, and readings, this live event will celebrate the diverse voices and creative talent of local young people.

Title: Olga Ravn: A Writer at Work
Teaser: With the irresistible International Booker Prize-shortlisted The Employees, Danish novelist Olga Ravn proved she can take an everyday experience – working – and reframe it as something quietly revolutionary. Now she returns with My Work, a funny and...
Description: With the irresistible International Booker Prize-shortlisted The Employees, Danish novelist Olga Ravn proved she can take an everyday experience – working – and reframe it as something quietly revolutionary. Now she returns with My Work, a funny and mercilessly honest novel about motherhood. Weaving together prose, poetry, journal entries, and letters, Ravn creates a compulsive examination of the emotions around motherhood – and of the love and pain it brings. In conversation with Chitra Ramaswamy.

Title: Cariad Lloyd: Lessons from Loss
Teaser: Aged 15, Cariad Lloyd became someone she never wanted to be: a person-whose-dad-had-died. Years later, she began a podcast, Griefcast, to examine her grief and provide comfort and candour to others. Death is something that connects us all, despite our...
Description: Aged 15, Cariad Lloyd became someone she never wanted to be: a person-whose-dad-had-died. Years later, she began a podcast, Griefcast, to examine her grief and provide comfort and candour to others. Death is something that connects us all, despite our different cultural ways of processing it. In You Are Not Alone, Lloyd reflects on grief in all its sad, surprising, awkward, tender, and sometimes funny forms. In conversation with Roxani Krystalli.

Title: Samanta Schweblin: Home Bittersweet Home
Teaser: She may be at the forefront of a talented generation of Latin American writers, but Samanta Schweblin is one of a kind and her short story collection, Seven Empty Houses, has won a National Book Award in the USA to prove it. Her stories show exactly why...
Description: She may be at the forefront of a talented generation of Latin American writers, but Samanta Schweblin is one of a kind and her short story collection, Seven Empty Houses, has won a National Book Award in the USA to prove it. Her stories show exactly why Schweblin gained international fame: set in a series of domestic spaces, each vignette is shot through with delicious unease. In conversation with Kirsty Logan.

Title: Sarah Krasnostein & Dina Nayeri: Beyond Belief
Teaser: Following the success of The Trauma Cleaner, Sarah Krasnostein's new book, The Believer, speaks to ordinary people who believe extraordinary things and examines how these stories impact our lives. Academic and award-winning author of The Ungrateful...
Description: Following the success of The Trauma Cleaner, Sarah Krasnostein's new book, The Believer, speaks to ordinary people who believe extraordinary things and examines how these stories impact our lives. Academic and award-winning author of The Ungrateful Refugee, Dina Nayeri combines deep reportage with her own life experience in the profound book Who Gets Believed? Both books ask: who and what do we believe – and why? Chaired by Roxani Krystalli.

Title: Jenny Colgan: Flights Of Fancy
Teaser: Having sold more than 9 million copies of her books around the world, Jenny Colgan's writing is characteristically funny, romantic, and irresistibly warm. For her legions of fans, there’s the special recognition that her books are set in the Scottish...
Description: Having sold more than 9 million copies of her books around the world, Jenny Colgan's writing is characteristically funny, romantic, and irresistibly warm. For her legions of fans, there’s the special recognition that her books are set in the Scottish isles. Colgan talks with Sally Magnusson about her new book The Summer Skies, featuring the capers of Morag, a pilot who ferries locals across the islands of a Scottish archipelago.

Title: Scots Rhymetimes with Craigmillar Books for Babies
Teaser: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies as they celebrate their 25th anniversary with a special Scots Rhymetime! Enjoy Scots rhymes, songs, lots of cuddles, and fun to support attachment and bonding with your wee ones.
Description: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies as they celebrate their 25th anniversary with a special Scots Rhymetime! Enjoy Scots rhymes, songs, lots of cuddles, and fun to support attachment and bonding with your wee ones.

Title: Baby and Toddler Rhymetime with Craigmillar Books for Babies
Teaser: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies as they celebrate their 25th anniversary with a special Baby and Toddler Rhymetime. Enjoy bouncy songs, tickly rhymes, lots of cuddles, and fun to help build attachment and bonding with your little ones.
Description: Join Craigmillar Books for Babies as they celebrate their 25th anniversary with a special Baby and Toddler Rhymetime. Enjoy bouncy songs, tickly rhymes, lots of cuddles, and fun to help build attachment and bonding with your little ones.

Title: Baby and Toddler Rhymetime with Craigmillar Books for Babies

Teaser: Join local community early literacy project Craigmillar Books for Babies as they celebrate their 25th anniversary with a special Baby and Toddler Rhymetime. There will be bouncy songs, tickly rhymes, lots of cuddles, and fun to help build attachment and...
