Title: Mikaela Loach: Changing the Climate Narrative
Teaser: Edinburgh-based Mikaela Loach is a climate justice activist, podcaster, and writer who campaigns for a climate movement which is both inclusive and intersectional. Her new book, It’s Not That Radical, is one of candour and hope, bringing a fresh and...
Description: Edinburgh-based Mikaela Loach is a climate justice activist, podcaster, and writer who campaigns for a climate movement which is both inclusive and intersectional. Her new book, It’s Not That Radical, is one of candour and hope, bringing a fresh and far-reaching perspective which advocates for real climate action. Gemma Cairney speaks to Loach in an inspiring discussion of how it’s not too late to enact change.

Title: Camilla Grudova & Olga Ravn: I Do Not Dream of Labour
Teaser: From quiet quitting to strike action, work has occupied recent news headlines. Exploring the anxiety, intimacy, and strangeness of the workplace, Camilla Grudova’s Children of Paradise is set at an independent cinema which rebels against being...
Description: From quiet quitting to strike action, work has occupied recent news headlines. Exploring the anxiety, intimacy, and strangeness of the workplace, Camilla Grudova’s Children of Paradise is set at an independent cinema which rebels against being acquired by a chain corporation. Olga Ravn’s follow-up to her International Booker Prize-shortlisted The Employees, is My Work, which blends prose and poetry to examine the labour of rearing children and creating art. In conversation with Kirsty Logan.

Title: Colin Grant & Chitra Ramaswamy: Lives of Others
Teaser: What can telling someone else’s story tell you about yourself? Chitra Ramaswamy’s Homelands and Colin Grant’s I’m Black So You Don’t Have To Be explore exactly that. These writers have created delicate portraits which hover between biography...
Description: What can telling someone else’s story tell you about yourself? Chitra Ramaswamy’s Homelands and Colin Grant’s I’m Black So You Don’t Have To Be explore exactly that. These writers have created delicate portraits which hover between biography and memoir, intermixing their own narratives with those of friends and family. Together they discuss belonging, family histories, and the need to tell their stories with Esa Aldegheri.

Title: Katie Holten & Katie Paterson: Rewilding Stories
Teaser: Irish artist and environmental activist Katie Holten creates unconventional works that intersect ecology, language, and history, including The Language of Trees. Scottish artist Katie Paterson's work emphasises nature, geology, and cosmology – she has...
Description: Irish artist and environmental activist Katie Holten creates unconventional works that intersect ecology, language, and history, including The Language of Trees. Scottish artist Katie Paterson's work emphasises nature, geology, and cosmology – she has created a library for the future, recorded melting glaciers, and compiled an archive of darkness from the depths of the Universe. Join these two artists as they talk about creativity and wonder. Chaired by Sophie Cunningham.

Title: Shushan Avagyan & Sophie Cunningham: Imagined Encounters
Teaser: What does it mean to translate history? Where do the boundaries between the past and the present lie? And what happens when a writer slips through these supposedly rigid lines? These questions and more are explored in Shushan Avagyan’s poetic work of...
Description:
What does it mean to translate history? Where do the boundaries between the past and the present lie? And what happens when a writer slips through these supposedly rigid lines? These questions and more are explored in Shushan Avagyan’s poetic work of translated autofiction, A Book, Untitled, and Sophie Cunningham’s This Devastating Fever, a novel which brings Leonard Woolf and Y2K together in dazzling ways. Chaired by Catherine Wilson.

	Please note: Shushan Avagyan will now be appearing remotely.

Title: Iman Mersal: A Portrait from the Archives
Teaser: Celebrated poet, writer, academic, and translator, Iman Mersal was born in the northern Egyptian Delta before emigrating to Canada. Mersal shares a wide-ranging exploration of the life of revered Egyptian writer, Enayat Al Zayyat, who died by suicide...
Description: Celebrated poet, writer, academic, and translator, Iman Mersal was born in the northern Egyptian Delta before emigrating to Canada. Mersal shares a wide-ranging exploration of the life of revered Egyptian writer, Enayat Al Zayyat, who died by suicide at the age of 27. Traces of Enayat, published in Arabic in 2019, translated by Robin Moger, is not only a biography: it’s a memoir, a detective story, and a compelling portrait of life for women in Egypt. In conversation with Mohamed Tonsy.

Title: Jokha Alharthi: The James Tait Black Event
Teaser: Jokha Alharthi became the first Omani woman writer to be translated into English for her 2019 International Booker Prize-winning work Celestial Bodies. Her exquisite follow-up, Bitter Orange Tree, is among the eight exceptional books shortlisted for...
Description: Jokha Alharthi became the first Omani woman writer to be translated into English for her 2019 International Booker Prize-winning work Celestial Bodies. Her exquisite follow-up, Bitter Orange Tree, is among the eight exceptional books shortlisted for this year’s James Tait Black Prizes, the only major prize to be judged by scholars and students. Join Alharthi and her translator Marilyn Booth in conversation with lead fiction judge, Benjamin Bateman, to find out what set this book apart.

Title: Ali Smith: The Writer's Art
Teaser: With the completion of her Seasonal Quartet novels and the accompanying Companion Piece, Ali Smith underlined her striking ability to portray personal encounters and relationships alongside the limpid portrayal of a fast-changing British society. The...
Description: With the completion of her Seasonal Quartet novels and the accompanying Companion Piece, Ali Smith underlined her striking ability to portray personal encounters and relationships alongside the limpid portrayal of a fast-changing British society. The novels are simultaneously rooted in contemporary life and flights of pure imagination. As the Book Festival celebrates its 40th anniversary, Smith looks back over key events in her life as a writer, exploring the ways they sparked her fiction with Sarah Wood.

Title: Claire Askew & Kate Foster: Tales of Two Edinburghs
Teaser: What is it about the Scottish capital that makes it such fertile ground for fictionalised mystery? Claire Askew’s The Dead Don’t Speak sees DI Helen Birch drawn back into action when an anonymous vigilante starts stalking the streets of Edinburgh....
Description: What is it about the Scottish capital that makes it such fertile ground for fictionalised mystery? Claire Askew’s The Dead Don’t Speak sees DI Helen Birch drawn back into action when an anonymous vigilante starts stalking the streets of Edinburgh. Kate Foster’s thriller, The Maiden, is inspired by the real-life trial of a 17th century Edinburgh woman charged with murder. Join two writers securing Scotland’s reputation for world-class crime fiction. Chaired by Susan Mansfield.

Title: Caroline Moorehead: Mussolini’s Dangerous Daughter
Teaser: Where did power really lie in Fascist Italy? Not just with Benito Mussolini, according to Caroline Moorehead, but also with his favourite daughter. In the engrossing Edda Mussolini Moorehead the rise and fall of a woman whose husband, Galeazzo Ciano,...
Description: Where did power really lie in Fascist Italy? Not just with Benito Mussolini, according to Caroline Moorehead, but also with his favourite daughter. In the engrossing Edda Mussolini Moorehead examines the rise and fall of a woman whose husband, Galeazzo Ciano, was Foreign Minister before he plotted to bring Mussolini down.The celebrated biographer joins Jamie Jauncey to discuss this fascinating figure.

Title: Jenny Graham & Kate Rawles: A Better World on Two Wheels
Teaser: Jenny Graham and Kate Rawles are passionate about endurance cycling, but they’re just as interested in people, landscape, and the world around them. In Coffee First, Then the World, Graham tells the story of her record-breaking solo ride around the...
Description: Jenny Graham and Kate Rawles are passionate about endurance cycling, but they’re just as interested in people, landscape, and the world around them. In Coffee First, Then the World, Graham tells the story of her record-breaking solo ride around the world, while in The Life Cycle, Rawles recounts her 8,000 mile trek across South America on a bike made of bamboo. In this innovative event, you can hear them in conversation with fellow endurance cyclist Emily Chappell, and then (for a maximum of 32 people, for an additional charge) take part in a special bike ride with all three in the local area the following morning. For more details see edbookfest.co.uk/insideout.

Title: Damian Barr & Catherine Taylor: Strange Country of the North
Teaser: Damian Barr’s Maggie & Me is a bestselling memoir of growing up in Thatcher’s Britain. A decade since its publication, he returns to discuss that memorable period with Catherine Taylor whose own memoir, The Stirrings, offers her account of growing...
Description: Damian Barr’s Maggie & Me is a bestselling memoir of growing up in Thatcher’s Britain. A decade since its publication, he returns to discuss that memorable period with Catherine Taylor whose own memoir, The Stirrings, offers her account of growing up in 1970s and 80s Sheffield. Join us for a fascinating conversation between two writers exploring the hopes and fears of adolescence during that time. Chaired by Mary Robson.

Title: James Jauncey: The Gentleman Socialist
Teaser: Writer, prospector for gold, socialist: Robert Bontine Cunninghame Graham was one of a kind. Elected to Parliament in 1886 as a Liberal MP, he pursued a radical agenda, condemning child labour and capital punishment – and later co-founded the Scottish...
Description: Writer, prospector for gold, socialist: Robert Bontine Cunninghame Graham was one of a kind. Elected to Parliament in 1886 as a Liberal MP, he pursued a radical agenda, condemning child labour and capital punishment – and later co-founded the Scottish Labour Party with Keir Hardie. Upon failing to get elected in 1892, he went unsuccessfully in search of gold in Spain. Now, R B Cunninghame Graham’s great-great-nephew James Jauncey tells the story of the remarkable Don Roberto in conversation with Ruth Wishart.

Title: Monica Heisey: On Modern Love
Teaser: Newlywed PhD student Maggie is in her late 20s with her whole life ahead of her – and then her husband asks for a divorce, moves out, and takes the cat with him. Really Good, Actually is as hilarious and heartfelt as you’d expect from Monica...
Description: Newlywed PhD student Maggie is in her late 20s with her whole life ahead of her – and then her husband asks for a divorce, moves out, and takes the cat with him. Really Good, Actually is as hilarious and heartfelt as you’d expect from Monica Heisey, a screenwriter on the beloved television show Schitt’s Creek. Join her for an astute perspective on modern love with Nyla Ahmad.

Title: Kevin Jared Hosein & Fiona McFarlane: Missing Persons
Teaser: Two missing people spark profound change in colonial lands: 1940s Trinidad and 1800s Australia. In Kevin Jared Hosein's mesmerising Hungry Ghosts, an overseer's disappearance forever changes a small community. In Fiona McFarlane's haunting and...
Description: Two missing people spark profound change in colonial lands: 1940s Trinidad and 1800s Australia. In Kevin Jared Hosein's mesmerising Hungry Ghosts, an overseer's disappearance forever changes a small community. In Fiona McFarlane's haunting and atmospheric The Sun Walks Down, a six year old boy could be found, or lost forever. Hear these award winning authors discuss their work with Michael Williams. Please note, Kevin Jared Hosein will appear remotely.

Title: Angela Saini & Gary Younge: Power and Protest
Teaser: Gary Younge’s Dispatches From The Diaspora vividly documents race, racism, Black life and death, and the changes he has witnessed throughout his journalistic career. In The Patriarchs, Angela Saini examines the origins of patriarchy, and exposes its...
Description:
Gary Younge’s Dispatches From The Diaspora vividly documents race, racism, Black life and death, and the changes he has witnessed throughout his journalistic career. In The Patriarchs, Angela Saini examines the origins of patriarchy, and exposes its fragility. Join us as two of Britain’s foremost journalists discuss global power dynamics, and share their thoughts on who has it, who doesn’t, and how it can be wrested back.

	Chaired by Lucia Osborne-Crowley.

Title: Val McDermid: A Life in Writing
Teaser: As the Book Festival celebrates its 40th anniversary, Val McDermid talks to Peggy Hughes about her work, and looks back over key events in her life as a writer, exploring the ways in which they have sparked her fiction. Alongside McDermid’s...
Description: As the Book Festival celebrates its 40th anniversary, Val McDermid talks to Peggy Hughes about her work, and looks back over key events in her life as a writer, exploring the ways in which they have sparked her fiction. Alongside McDermid’s bestselling series featuring DCI Karen Pirie, there’s 1979 and 1989 - the first novels of a new series charting the adventures of her latest fictional icon, Allie Burns.

Title: James Crawford, Ben Judah & Kapka Kassabova: Crossing Borders
Teaser: Alongside the powerful human urge to create borders, there seems to be an equally strong urge to make connections and transcend them. James Crawford’s The Edge of the Plain, Ben Judah’s This Is Europe, and Kapka Kassabova’s Border: A Journey to...
Description: Alongside the powerful human urge to create borders, there seems to be an equally strong urge to make connections and transcend them. James Crawford’s The Edge of the Plain, Ben Judah’s This Is Europe, and Kapka Kassabova’s Border: A Journey to the Edge of Europe each address the psychological boundaries that divide us, and the human links we forge. Today they discuss boundaries in prose and outlook.

Title: Future Library Announcement: Future Writer, Future Readers
Teaser: Since 2014, authors have contributed to Future Library, a collection of writing that will not be published for 100 years. The venerable group includes Margaret Atwood, David Mitchell, Han Kang, and Judith Schalansky. This project was conceived by artist...
Description: Since 2014, authors have contributed to Future Library, a collection of writing that will not be published for 100 years. The venerable group includes Margaret Atwood, David Mitchell, Han Kang, and Judith Schalansky. This project was conceived by artist Katie Paterson, and supported by the City of Oslo. Join Paterson, Schalansky, and Future Library Trust chairwoman Anne Beate Hovind as they discuss the project, and announce the next writer. Chaired by Cal Flyn.

Title: Irene Vallejo: The Joy of Books
Teaser: What happens inside our heads when we open a book and read? Spanish journalist and philologist Irene Vallejo has turned her passion for books into an evocative and rich history. Beginning in libraries in the ancient world and with references ranging...
Description: What happens inside our heads when we open a book and read? Spanish journalist and philologist Irene Vallejo has turned her passion for books into an evocative and rich history. Beginning in libraries in the ancient world and with references ranging from Plato to Orwell, Papyrus, translated into English by Charlotte Whittle, was a major bestseller in Spain. Today Vallejo talks about her extraordinary work with Daniel Hahn.

Title: Elif Shafak: A Life in the Imagination
Teaser: When her twelfth novel, The Island of Missing Trees, was published recently, Elif Shafak turned her luminous imagination to life in Cyprus – both for its people and for a fig tree living there. That novel reflects Shafak’s enduring interest in...
Description:
When her twelfth novel, The Island of Missing Trees, was published recently, Elif Shafak turned her luminous imagination to life in Cyprus – both for its people and for a fig tree living there. That novel reflects Shafak’s enduring interest in roots, belonging, and identity even in troubled environments. As the Book Festival celebrates its 40th anniversary, Shafak discusses her latest book and looks back over key events in her life as a writer.

	In conversation with Sam Baker.

Title: Sebastian Faulks: Before You Were Born
Teaser: Thirty years after the publication of Sebastian Faulks’s breakthrough bestseller Birdsong, we welcome him back to Edinburgh to launch his much-anticipated new novel The Seventh Son. Sweeping between New York, London, and the Scottish Highlands, this...
Description: Thirty years after the publication of Sebastian Faulks’s breakthrough bestseller Birdsong, we welcome him back to Edinburgh to launch his much-anticipated new novel The Seventh Son. Sweeping between New York, London, and the Scottish Highlands, this is an ethical riddle of love, science, and power. Join Faulks in conversation with Stuart Kelly about this landmark work in a stellar literary career.

Title: Stephen Buoro & Chika Unigwe: Growing Pains
Teaser: Two fascinating coming-of-age novelists focus on love, agency, and resilience within Nigerian families. Stephen Buoro was the subject of an eight-way auction for his dazzling debut novel The Five Sorrowful Mysteries of Andy Africa. He’s joined on...
Description: Two fascinating coming-of-age novelists focus on love, agency, and resilience within Nigerian families. Stephen Buoro was the subject of an eight-way auction for his dazzling debut novel The Five Sorrowful Mysteries of Andy Africa. He’s joined on stage by US-based Chika Unigwe, whose unforgettable latest, The Middle Daughter, examines the challenges facing a 17 year old woman in a patriarchal society. In conversation with Tomiwa Folorunso.

Title: Ian Goldin & Tom Lee-Devlin: Why Cities Will Define Our Future
Teaser: The city is the supreme symbol of human endeavour and, according to the authors of Age of the City, the place where the key threats to human sustainability must be faced. Ian Goldin is a world-leading voice on globalisation and development. Tom...
Description: The city is the supreme symbol of human endeavour and, according to the authors of Age of the City, the place where the key threats to human sustainability must be faced. Ian Goldin is a world-leading voice on globalisation and development. Tom Lee-Devlin is global business correspondent for the Economist. Here, they explain why cities are where the battles of inequality, social division, pandemics, and climate change will be fought. In conversation with Jude Barber.

Title: Brian Dillon: Exploring Our Affinities
Teaser: We are bombarded by thousands of images every day, but why are we drawn to particular photographs, objects, and artists? Award-winning author, curator and academic Brian Dillon grapples with this idea in Affinities, a fascinating series of personal and...
Description: We are bombarded by thousands of images every day, but why are we drawn to particular photographs, objects, and artists? Award-winning author, curator and academic Brian Dillon grapples with this idea in Affinities, a fascinating series of personal and critical essays. Here, he reflects on what feelings of affinity can tell us about our individual and collective experience of art, and of the world today, with Fiona Bradley.

Title: Polly Toynbee: By the Byline
Teaser: How does Polly Toynbee square a family history which includes a stately home spotted in several period dramas with her place in a long line of committed left-wing rabble rousers? Hear the much-loved Guardian writer discuss her memoir An Uneasy...
Description: How does Polly Toynbee square a family history which includes a stately home spotted in several period dramas with her place in a long line of committed left-wing rabble rousers? Hear the much-loved Guardian writer discuss her memoir An Uneasy Inheritance: My Family and Other Radicals, exploring the guilt of privilege, the myth of mobility, and the complexities of class in Britain now. In conversation with Sally Magnusson.

Title: Linda Cracknell & Noreen Masud: Landscape and Bodies
Teaser: Muddy boots, the chill of a snowy forest and the slap of saltwater: in Writing Landscape, Linda Cracknell’s essay collection, she channels the natural world through the physical body. Noreen Masud’s debut memoir, A Flat Place, encourages us to see...
Description: Muddy boots, the chill of a snowy forest and the slap of saltwater: in Writing Landscape, Linda Cracknell’s essay collection, she channels the natural world through the physical body. Noreen Masud’s debut memoir, A Flat Place, encourages us to see bare expanses of flatlands not as haunted places, but as alive with significance and healing in the wake of trauma. Join two authors bringing us closer to the natural world. Chaired by Jessica Gaitán Johannesson.

Title: Chris Bryant & Representative for Belarusian Political Prisoners: Europe – The Precarity of Democracy
Teaser: Labour MP Chris Bryant, as chair of the Committee of Standards, is tasked with cleaning up Westminster’s act. Today he speaks with a representative from one of the main political prisoner support NGOs in Poland who has worked beside Maxim Znak, the...
Description: Labour MP Chris Bryant, as chair of the Committee of Standards, is tasked with cleaning up Westminster’s act. Today he speaks with a representative from one of the main political prisoner support NGOs in Poland who has worked beside Maxim Znak, the imprisoned Belarusian lawyer and author of The Zekameron. What can champions of democracy learn from other political systems? Join today’s open-minded discussion, chaired by Allan Little.

Title: Matty Long: Super Happy Drawing Time
Teaser: Come on an epic drawing adventure with Matty Long as he takes you through the magical world of his Super Happy Magic Forest series. Exploding with fun, the tales follow five unlikely heroes embarking on a quest to save their home. Join...
Description: Come on an epic drawing adventure with Matty Long as he takes you through the magical world of his Super Happy Magic Forest series. Exploding with fun, the tales follow five unlikely heroes embarking on a quest to save their home. Join author-illustrator Matty to find out more about what his hilarious characters get up to, before getting a step-by-step guide on how to draw them yourself.

Title: David Farrier & Karine Polwart: Different Futures are Possible
Teaser: Through literature, art, and science, David Farrier’s Footprints: In Search of Future Fossils asks what generations would find of today’s ecological crisis in the distant future. Musician Karine Polwart is also deeply interested in place as a site...
Description: Through literature, art, and science, David Farrier’s Footprints: In Search of Future Fossils asks what generations would find of today’s ecological crisis in the distant future. Musician Karine Polwart is also deeply interested in place as a site for hidden histories, scientific curiosity, and folklore. Join us today as they discuss how to transform planning for the future, with Jessica Gaitán Johannesson.

Title: Victoria Belim & Emmanuel Iduma: Lost Legacies, Hidden Histories
Teaser: Authors Victoria Belim and Emmanuel Iduma share their personal, moving experiences, discussing the interplay between global forces and personal histories. They have a dogged shared commitment to unearthing the past - Belim in The Rooster House, tying...
Description: Authors Victoria Belim and Emmanuel Iduma share their personal, moving experiences, discussing the interplay between global forces and personal histories. They have a dogged shared commitment to unearthing the past - Belim in The Rooster House, tying family secrets to Ukraine's hidden history; and Iduma in I Am Still With You, part-memoir, part-political reckoning tracing his roots amongst those displaced by the Nigerian Civil War. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

Title: Jen Calleja & William Letford: Poetic Dystopian Futures
Teaser: Jen Calleja’s striking new verse novel, Vehicle, constructs a dystopian world where fugitive researchers try to piece together their collective story of a disaster that occurred fifty years earlier. Scottish poet William Letford transports us to a...
Description: Jen Calleja’s striking new verse novel, Vehicle, constructs a dystopian world where fugitive researchers try to piece together their collective story of a disaster that occurred fifty years earlier. Scottish poet William Letford transports us to a not-too-distant future in his long-anticipated From Our Own Fire, in which artificial intelligence rules the world. Two fresh poetic voices come together to share their insights into past, present, and future. Chaired by Andrés N Ordorica.

Title: Lauren Elkin: The Body as a Canvas
Teaser: Reclaiming the representation of the female body; giving a new definition to the aesthetic aims of art which represents all bodies: this is the radical heritage of feminist art, and the terrain of Art Monsters, a landmark book by Lauren Elkin. Described...
Description: Reclaiming the representation of the female body; giving a new definition to the aesthetic aims of art which represents all bodies: this is the radical heritage of feminist art, and the terrain of Art Monsters, a landmark book by Lauren Elkin. Described by Deborah Levy as ‘the Susan Sontag of her generation’, Elkin accompanies us into a world of ‘unruly bodies’. In conversation with Katrina Brown.

Title: Sara Pascoe: Why Be Normal When You Can Be Funny?
Teaser: Much loved comedian, actor, TV personality, and writer Sara Pascoe has enlightened readers – and made them howl with laughter – with her reflections on femininity and sexuality in non-fiction books Animal and Sex Power Money. Now, she turns her...
Description: Much loved comedian, actor, TV personality, and writer Sara Pascoe has enlightened readers – and made them howl with laughter – with her reflections on femininity and sexuality in non-fiction books Animal and Sex Power Money. Now, she turns her talents to fiction with Weirdo, the tale of a woman desperate to seem like a ‘normal’, well-adjusted grown up. If only she could stop the voices in her head. In converstation with Michael Pedersen.

Title: Linton Kwesi Johnson: Perspectives in Prose
Teaser: One of the great poets of our times, Linton Kwesi Johnson has been highly influential in reflecting and understanding modern Britain. The publication of Time Come, a prose collection, demonstrates that his non-fiction voice is equally powerful and...
Description: One of the great poets of our times, Linton Kwesi Johnson has been highly influential in reflecting and understanding modern Britain. The publication of Time Come, a prose collection, demonstrates that his non-fiction voice is equally powerful and persuasive. Drawing on Johnson’s Jamaican roots and on wider Caribbean history, these writings offer an essential perspective on culture, politics, and ideas over the past half century. Chaired by Zaffar Kunial.

Title: Polly Morland & Rebecca Smith: Landscape and Community
Teaser: Polly Morland’s A Fortunate Woman explores 50 years of seismic change in our society through one woman’s remarkable life. Rebecca Smith’s Rural: The Lives of the Working-Class Countryside expands out from her own family history to show how those...
Description: Polly Morland’s A Fortunate Woman explores 50 years of seismic change in our society through one woman’s remarkable life. Rebecca Smith’s Rural: The Lives of the Working-Class Countryside expands out from her own family history to show how those who labour in nature often have the least control over what happens there. This is for anybody who aches for what has been lost.

Title: Mat Osman: The Fickle Friend of Fortune
Teaser: A founding member of Suede and the brother of chart-topping crime fiction sensation Richard Osman, Mat Osman visits Edinburgh to discuss his hugely exciting second book The Ghost Theatre. A dazzling punk re-imagining of Elizabethan London, this...
Description: A founding member of Suede and the brother of chart-topping crime fiction sensation Richard Osman, Mat Osman visits Edinburgh to discuss his hugely exciting second book The Ghost Theatre. A dazzling punk re-imagining of Elizabethan London, this historical novel tells its gripping story through the eyes of a clairvoyant, bird-worshipping protagonist and her unlikely theatre troupe. In conversation with Rodge Glass.

Title: Shehan Karunatilaka: Where Your Imagination Can Go
Teaser: In October 2022, Shehan Karunatilaka’s life changed forever when his novel was announced as the newest winner of the Booker Prize. Praised by one reviewer as ‘relentlessly, shockingly funny’, The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida is a hugely enjoyable...
Description: In October 2022, Shehan Karunatilaka’s life changed forever when his novel was announced as the newest winner of the Booker Prize. Praised by one reviewer as ‘relentlessly, shockingly funny’, The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida is a hugely enjoyable story set in 1980s Colombo – and in a parallel afterlife where Maali finds himself. Today Karunatilaka explains the background to his novel, dicussing life, death, and the echoes of civil war in Sri Lanka with Bidisha Mamata.

Title: Munroe Bergdorf: Transformations
Teaser: Activist, model, author, broadcaster and British Vogue contributing editor, Munroe Bergdorf is used to breaking new ground. For her work campaigning for transgender rights, she was appointed a National Advocate, UN Women Changemaker for UN Women UK in...
Description: Activist, model, author, broadcaster and British Vogue contributing editor, Munroe Bergdorf is used to breaking new ground. For her work campaigning for transgender rights, she was appointed a National Advocate, UN Women Changemaker for UN Women UK in 2019. In her first book, Transitional, Bergdorf shares personal reflections and proposes that we are constantly in transition as we move through the world. Join Gemma Cairney as she speaks to Bergdorf about how our differences can be used to strengthen our community.

Title: Is This a Good Time to Be Writing for Children?
Teaser: What are Scottish publishers looking for in a children’s book today? And what can authors and illustrators do to stand out against the myriad of manuscripts sent to literary agents every day? Join Sally Polson of Floris Books, Alan Windram of Little...
Description: What are Scottish publishers looking for in a children’s book today? And what can authors and illustrators do to stand out against the myriad of manuscripts sent to literary agents every day? Join Sally Polson of Floris Books, Alan Windram of Little Door Books, and Lindsey Fraser of Fraser Ross Associates Literary Agents, for an illuminating panel discussion. Chaired by network organiser for SCBWI Scotland, Caroline Deacon.

Title: Yiyun Li: Beware the Golden Goose
Teaser: From the acclaimed author of Where Reasons End and Dear Friend, From My Life I Write to You in Your Life comes The Book of Goose. Set between rural France, an English boarding school, and Pennsylvania, this is a subversive and darkly powerful story of...
Description: From the acclaimed author of Where Reasons End and Dear Friend, From My Life I Write to You in Your Life comes The Book of Goose. Set between rural France, an English boarding school, and Pennsylvania, this is a subversive and darkly powerful story of intimacy, obsession, friendship, and rivalry. Join Daniel Hahn for a riveting conversation with a writer at the height of her powers.

Title: Rebecca May Johnson: Kitchen Confessional
Teaser: Food isn’t simply fuel: it’s a vehicle for life. Editor, writer, and essayist Rebecca May Johnson has shaken the culinary writing world up with Small Fires, mixing memoir with social criticism. Described by Nigella Lawson as ‘an intense,...
Description: Food isn’t simply fuel: it’s a vehicle for life. Editor, writer, and essayist Rebecca May Johnson has shaken the culinary writing world up with Small Fires, mixing memoir with social criticism. Described by Nigella Lawson as ‘an intense, thought-provoking enquiry into the very nature of cooking', this work of meditation and memory speaks to all. Join her in exploring how deeply food shapes our lives. In conversation with Nyla Ahmad.

Title: Lisa Croft, Willy Maley, Jennie Renton & Tam Watters: ¡No Pasaran!
Teaser: Our Fathers Fought Franco is the remarkable collective biography of four men - three from Scotland, and one from England - who enlisted in the XV International Brigade and fought in the Spanish Civil War. In 1937, they were in the battle of Jarama,...
Description: Our Fathers Fought Franco is the remarkable collective biography of four men - three from Scotland, and one from England - who enlisted in the XV International Brigade and fought in the Spanish Civil War. In 1937, they were in the battle of Jarama, ending up in the same prison cell. The authors have sifted through news reports, interviews, and prison diaries to explore why their ancestors set out to stand up against fascism. Chaired by Brian Taylor.

Title: Sarah Polley: What I Run Towards Will Strengthen Me
Teaser: The 2023 Oscar-winning film adaptation of Miriam Toews’s novel Women Talking has brought its director Sarah Polley international attention. Alongside it the Toronto-based writer-director has written Run Towards the Danger, a collection of essays about...
Description: The 2023 Oscar-winning film adaptation of Miriam Toews’s novel Women Talking has brought its director Sarah Polley international attention. Alongside it the Toronto-based writer-director has written Run Towards the Danger, a collection of essays about her life. From making peace with her early life to the challenging process of recovering from an intense concussion, Polley joins us remotely to discuss her work and ideas. In conversation with Jackie Wylie.

Title: David Farrier & Katherine Rundell: Creature Future
Teaser: David Farrier, author of Footprints: In Search of Future Fossils, captures what nature can teach us about life on a human planet in his forthcoming book Curious Earth. Writer Katherine Rundell has catalogued nature’s brilliant and endangered creatures...
Description: David Farrier, author of Footprints: In Search of Future Fossils, captures what nature can teach us about life on a human planet in his forthcoming book Curious Earth. Writer Katherine Rundell has catalogued nature’s brilliant and endangered creatures in The Golden Mole, a litany of what makes this world worth fighting for. Join Farrier and Rundell as they reckon with what we risk losing to rapid change. In conversation with Dan Richards.

Title: Katherine Rundell: John Donne, Undone
Teaser: Super-infinite, Katherine Rundell’s wondrous biography of John Donne, won the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction last year. This deeply thoughtful work enables the reader to scale the cosmic heights of the poet's original mind and to understand the...
Description: Super-infinite, Katherine Rundell’s wondrous biography of John Donne, won the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction last year. This deeply thoughtful work enables the reader to scale the cosmic heights of the poet's original mind and to understand the times in which he lived. Today she discusses a new essay for the Book Festival, introducing Donne’s main themes and close reading one of his poems. In conversation with Gavin Francis.

Title: Isabella Hammad & Cecile Pin: Love and Displacement
Teaser: Hear two novelists grapple with love, ancestry, and fragmented lives in their latest works. Enter Ghost by Isabella Hammad is a moving tale set in Palestine, exploring family connections, art, and shared resistance. Cecile Pin’s debut, Wandering...
Description: Hear two novelists grapple with love, ancestry, and fragmented lives in their latest works. Enter Ghost by Isabella Hammad is a moving tale set in Palestine, exploring family connections, art, and shared resistance. Cecile Pin’s debut, Wandering Souls, tells the story of three Vietnamese siblings who seek refuge in the UK. In what is sure to be a fascinating conversation, hear from two powerful voices in contemporary fiction. Chaired by Katie Goh.

Title: Nicole Flattery: Factory or Fiction
Teaser: Hear Nicole Flattery discuss her funny and wildly inventive debut novel, Nothing Special, the follow-up to acclaimed short story collection, Show Them a Good Time. Attending high school by day and partying with the Velvet Underground by night, the novel...
Description: Hear Nicole Flattery discuss her funny and wildly inventive debut novel, Nothing Special, the follow-up to acclaimed short story collection, Show Them a Good Time. Attending high school by day and partying with the Velvet Underground by night, the novel centres on a teenager in 1960s New York who finds herself suddenly welcomed into the heart of Andy Warhol’s Factory. In conversation with Casi Dylan.

Title: Sara Baume & Kapka Kassabova: Nature’s Alchemy
Teaser: When we listen more closely to the natural world, what do we learn about ourselves? Sara Baume’s novel Seven Steeples is the tender story of two people living a life dictated by the seasons and nature. Meanwhile Kapka Kassabova travelled down the...
Description: When we listen more closely to the natural world, what do we learn about ourselves? Sara Baume’s novel Seven Steeples is the tender story of two people living a life dictated by the seasons and nature. Meanwhile Kapka Kassabova travelled down the Mesta River valley in Bulgaria for her sublime non-fiction book Elixir, learning from foragers, healers, and mystics who enjoy a symbiotic relationship with nature. Chaired by Jessica Gaitán Johannesson.

Title: Devorah Baum, Alva Gotby & Sophie K Rosa: Close Encounters
Teaser: Our most intimate moments – falling in love, marriage, raising children – are also some of our most political. Join these three powerful non-fiction writers as they interrogate the radical potential of intimacy. Devorah Baum’s On Marriage explores...
Description: Our most intimate moments – falling in love, marriage, raising children – are also some of our most political. Join these three powerful non-fiction writers as they interrogate the radical potential of intimacy. Devorah Baum’s On Marriage explores the contradictions of matrimony; Alva Gotby’s They Call It Love confronts emotional labour as a feminist issue; and Sophie K Rosa’s Radical Intimacy offers new frameworks for connection beyond capitalism. Chaired by Kevin Guyan.

Title: Chris Bryant: Can We Fix Westminster?
Teaser: Chris Bryant, Labour MP and chair of the Committee on Standards, joins us to discuss his new book, Code of Conduct: an examination of parliamentary conduct – from Boris Johnson’s lies, to Owen Paterson’s paid lobbying, to accusations of bullying...
Description: Chris Bryant, Labour MP and chair of the Committee on Standards, joins us to discuss his new book, Code of Conduct: an examination of parliamentary conduct – from Boris Johnson’s lies, to Owen Paterson’s paid lobbying, to accusations of bullying – that attempts to explain how things got so bad, while suggesting ways in which the problem may be fixed. In conversation with Ruth Wishart.

Title: Heather Parry & Em Strang: Back To Life
Teaser: In Heather Parry’s chilling debut Orpheus Builds a Girl, a woman presents her side of the story against the scientist who – with nobody’s permission – has brought her sister back from the dead.  In renowned poet Em Strang’s Quinn, a mother...
Description: In Heather Parry’s chilling debut Orpheus Builds a Girl, a woman presents her side of the story against the scientist who – with nobody’s permission – has brought her sister back from the dead. In renowned poet Em Strang’s Quinn, a mother opens her home to her daughter’s killer, recently released from prison. Join them for a conversation about autonomy and ownership with Harry Josephine Giles.

Title: William MacAskill: The Million Year View
Teaser: William MacAskill is an associate professor in philosophy at Oxford. In What We Owe the Future, he explores an idea currently fuelling the longtermist thinkers of the billionaire class: that we are remarkably early in the story of human civilization....
Description: Does what we do today determine the happiness or misery of trillions of people in the future? In this event, William MacAskill will discuss his recent book What We Owe the Future, and his argument for ‘longtermism’, which proposes that positively influencing the future is the moral priority of our time. MacAskill proposes that by making wise moral decisions today, we can navigate a multitude of crises – bioengineered pandemics, technological stagnation, climate change, and transformative AI – more fairly for generations to come. In conversation with David Farrier.

Title: Steven Isserlis & Sebastian Barry: Dancing With Bach
Teaser: If Johann Sebastian Bach was one of the 18th century’s greatest composers, then world-renowned cellist Steven Isserlis is the perfect interpreter today. In The Bach Cello Suites, Isserlis looks for the underlying narratives in these compositions,...
Description: If Johann Sebastian Bach was one of the 18th century’s greatest composers, then world-renowned cellist Steven Isserlis is the perfect interpreter today. In The Bach Cello Suites, Isserlis looks for the underlying narratives in these compositions, explaining why they are ripe for interpretation and reinterpretation now. Isserlis is joined by novelist Sebastian Barry, who will read excerpts while Isserlis plays from the suites. Chaired by Kate Molleson.

Title: Can Writers and Creators Help Communities Find Joy?
Teaser: In this poetry and panel event, we'll explore the non-fiction books inspiring joy in their readers and contributors. Following a poetry reading from Courtney Stoddart, we'll dive into an exciting panel discussion, and end the evening with a...
Description: In this poetry and panel event, we'll explore the non-fiction books inspiring joy in their readers and contributors. Following a poetry reading from Courtney Stoddart, we'll dive into an exciting panel discussion, and end the evening with a collaborative exercise led by Mikaela Loach, encouraging our audience to find joy in their own communities and personal lives. Hosted by Suzie Mwanza and Shirley McPherson, the stellar line up also includes Charlie Brinkhurst-Cuff, Timi Sotire, Zaki El-Salahi, and Anahit Behrooz. Please note: Mikaela Loach is no longer able to appear in this event.

Title: Michel Faber & Rodge Glass: Being Michel Faber
Teaser: His unorthodox, uncategorisable novels include Under The Skin and The Book of Strange New Things. Michel Faber is an author so influential and his life so unusual, that Rodge Glass has taken the smart step of writing a biography. Today, alongside Faber,...
Description: His unorthodox, uncategorisable novels include Under The Skin and The Book of Strange New Things. Michel Faber is an author so influential and his life so unusual, that Rodge Glass has taken the smart step of writing a biography. Today, alongside Faber, Glass presents Michel Faber: The Writer & His Work – a rare opportunity to hear a biographer in conversation with the subject of his book. Chaired by Michael Williams.

Title: Cecilia Knapp & Imogen West-Knights: Generation Games
Teaser: Two debuts unravel complex family dynamics and loss with wry humour. In Cecilia Knapp’s collection, Peach Pig, the former Young People’s Laureate for London explores the experience of motherlessness and grapples with grief passed between...
Description: Two debuts unravel complex family dynamics and loss with wry humour. In Cecilia Knapp’s collection, Peach Pig, the former Young People’s Laureate for London explores the experience of motherlessness and grapples with grief passed between generations. Imogen West-Knights’ novel Deep Down follows two estranged siblings who are thrown back together after the death of their father and must navigate their relationship while funeral planning in Paris. Chaired by Lucia Osborne-Crowley.

Title: Rob Delaney: An Open Heart
Teaser: Grief is something that we learn to live with in our own ways. Rob Delaney is a comedian and star of Catastrophe. He is also the father of Henry, who died after being diagnosed with a brain tumour when he was two. Somehow amidst the furious pain,...
Description: Grief is something that we learn to live with in our own ways. Rob Delaney is a comedian and star of Catastrophe. He is also the father of Henry, who died after being diagnosed with a brain tumour when he was two. Somehow amidst the furious pain, Delaney has written a memoir that is infused with humour and honesty. A Heart That Works is a testament to his craft as a writer, and his capacity as a person to share his story. He talks with Max Porter about writing and purpose.

Title: Sarah Bernstein & Sophie Mackintosh: Curious Incidents
Teaser: In any community, a series of unfortunate events can quickly escalate into a moral panic. The narrator of Sarah Bernstein’s Study for Obedience moves to a remote country and, according to suspicious locals, brings with her illness and blight. Based on...
Description: In any community, a series of unfortunate events can quickly escalate into a moral panic. The narrator of Sarah Bernstein’s Study for Obedience moves to a remote country and, according to suspicious locals, brings with her illness and blight. Based on a true story, Sophie Mackintosh’s Cursed Bread is about a baker’s wife who is bewitched by a charismatic new arrival while strange happenings plague their town. Chaired by Peggy Hughes.

Title: Marcas Mac an Tuairneir & Sam Ó Fearraigh: Languages of Poetry
Teaser: Gaelic and English language poet Marcas Mac an Tuairneir returns to the Festival with his poetry collection, Polaris – the word for 'languages' in the gay cryptolect Polari – alongside award-winning poet and dramaturg Sam Ó Fearraigh who writes in...
Description: Gaelic and English language poet Marcas Mac an Tuairneir returns to the Festival with his poetry collection, Polaris – the word for 'languages' in the gay cryptolect Polari – alongside award-winning poet and dramaturg Sam Ó Fearraigh who writes in English and Irish. Join these two astounding voices for a conversation about prioritising minoritised languages, and a celebration of identity across these islands. In conversation with Mohamed Tonsy.

Title: Jay Owens & Christopher Somerville: Geology and Hope
Teaser: Joining us in conversation are the authors of two new books on how geology can help us to understand and potentially mitigate the effects of climate change. Jay Owens’ Dust argues that dust is both the legacy of modern progress and a profound threat...
Description: Joining us in conversation are the authors of two new books on how geology can help us to understand and potentially mitigate the effects of climate change. Jay Owens’ Dust argues that dust is both the legacy of modern progress and a profound threat to future life, whereas Christopher Somerville’s Walking the Bones of Britain demystifies the unique geology of the British Isles. Chaired by Jo Sharp.

Title: Clemens Meyer & Claudia Piñeiro: From Leipzig to Buenos Aires
Teaser: Two giants of the international literary scene join us to discuss new English translations of their work. Clemens Meyer is the author of While We Were Dreaming, a passionate coming-of-age novel centering on a group of friends amidst the fall of the...
Description: Two giants of the international literary scene join us to discuss new English translations of their work. Clemens Meyer is the author of While We Were Dreaming, a passionate coming-of-age novel centering on a group of friends amidst the fall of the Berlin Wall, while A Little Luck is Claudia Piñeiro’s generation-spanning story of a Buenos Aires neighbourhood. Chaired by Daniel Hahn.

Title: Douglas MacIntyre, Grant McPhee, Hilary Morrison & Paul Research: We Oppose All Rock ‘n’ Roll
Teaser: Hungry Beat is a new, definitive oral history of two maverick independent music labels, Edinburgh's Fast Product and Glasgow's Postcard Records, and the Scottish post-punk era: 1977-1984. Join broadcaster Nicola Meighan for a conversation with author...
Description: Hungry Beat is a new, definitive oral history of two maverick independent music labels, Edinburgh's Fast Product and Glasgow's Postcard Records, and the Scottish post-punk era: 1977-1984. Join broadcaster Nicola Meighan for a conversation with author and musician Douglas MacIntyre, director Grant McPhee, Hilary Morrison from The Flowers, and Paul Research from Scars, followed by a live set with The Hungry Beat Group and guest vocalists.

Title: Fergal Keane with Allan Little: The Scars of War Reporting
Teaser: ‘The suffering of others was my daily bread.’ This brutally honest, heartfelt assessment of the job of a war reporter is central to Fergal Keane’s memoir, The Madness: a riveting account of how he survived war, fear, and PTSD, against a backdrop...
Description: ‘The suffering of others was my daily bread.’ This brutally honest, heartfelt assessment of the job of a war reporter is central to Fergal Keane’s memoir, The Madness: a riveting account of how he survived war, fear, and PTSD, against a backdrop of alcoholism and a troubled Irish history. Keane talks with fellow BBC reporter, Allan Little, about the importance of bearing witness and what drives foreign correspondents to risk their lives on the frontline.

Title: Victoria MacKenzie & Marion Turner: Positively Medieval
Teaser: Victoria MacKenzie’s debut novel, For Thy Great Pain Have Mercy On My Little Pain, circles Margery Kempe and Julian of Norwich, two extraordinary medieval women who experienced religious visions and were determined to preserve their own stories. Their...
Description: Victoria MacKenzie’s debut novel, For Thy Great Pain Have Mercy On My Little Pain, circles Margery Kempe and Julian of Norwich, two extraordinary medieval women who experienced religious visions and were determined to preserve their own stories. Their fictional contemporary is Chaucer’s bawdy pilgrim, The Wife of Bath, now the fascinating subject of Chaucer expert Marion Turner’s lifelong study. Hear how these stories have endured for over 600 years. Chaired by Kirsty Logan.

Title: Paul Johnson: How Much Does a Country Cost?
Teaser: The director of the IFS since 2011, Paul Johnson has been one of the most influential figures in British economic policy for decades. He joins us to discuss Follow The Money, which examines how the state raises and spends £1 trillion of our money every...
Description: The director of the IFS since 2011, Paul Johnson has been one of the most influential figures in British economic policy for decades. He joins us to discuss Follow The Money, which examines how the state raises and spends £1 trillion of our money every year, before explaining where the money comes from, where it goes to, and why it needs to change. Chaired by Columbia University Professor of History, Adam Tooze.

Title: Guy Gunaratne: Who Is Yahya Bas?
Teaser: Described by the Financial Times as one of the 30 most exciting young people on the planet, Guy Gunaratne follows up their lauded debut novel In Our Mad and Furious City with Mister, Mister, the story of a young poet who, while imprisoned in a British...
Description: Described by the Financial Times as one of the 30 most exciting young people on the planet, Guy Gunaratne follows up their lauded debut novel In Our Mad and Furious City with Mister, Mister, the story of a young poet who, while imprisoned in a British detention centre after fleeing the war in Syria, unwittingly finds himself becoming the voice of a generation. In conversation with Nikesh Shukla.

Title: Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀: The Price of Power
Teaser: Hear Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀ discussing A Spell of Good Things, a stunning novel where two families in 2000s Nigeria become tangled in a net of power, money, and political corruption. Ẹniọlá, a dreamer living in poverty, is a boy as tall as a...
Description: Hear Ayọ̀bámi Adébáyọ̀ discussing A Spell of Good Things, a stunning novel where two families in 2000s Nigeria become tangled in a net of power, money, and political corruption. Ẹniọlá, a dreamer living in poverty, is a boy as tall as a man who falls in with a local politician. Wúràọlá, the golden girl of a wealthy family, is a young doctor with a bright future. Hear how their story shines a light on modern Nigerian society. In conversation with Eilidh Akilade.

Title: Gerard Carruthers, Alan Riach & Sara Sheridan: Do We Need A New Canon?
Teaser: From Robert Louis Stevenson to Jackie Kay, Scotland has long been a beacon for great writing. Gerard Carruthers and Alan Riach, two of the country’s best-respected literature scholars, are joined today by writer and activist Sara Sheridan, bestselling...
Description: From Robert Louis Stevenson to Jackie Kay, Scotland has long been a beacon for great writing. Gerard Carruthers and Alan Riach, two of the country’s best-respected literature scholars, are joined today by writer and activist Sara Sheridan, bestselling author of The Fair Botanists, to discuss some of the nation’s greatest figures and their most influential texts – and who is missing from what we consider to be ‘canon’. Carruthers will be drawing on Scottish Stories, a new collection he edited, while Riach focuses on the influence of Hugh MacDiarmid as well as his new book Scottish Literature: An Introduction.

Title: Joanna Biggs: Life on the Line
Teaser: One day, Joanna Biggs took off her wedding ring for the last time. In A Life of One’s Own, she blends memoir and literary criticism to question domesticity, intellectual freedom, and traditional markers of womanhood. Through the lives of nine women...
Description: One day, Joanna Biggs took off her wedding ring for the last time. In A Life of One’s Own, she blends memoir and literary criticism to question domesticity, intellectual freedom, and traditional markers of womanhood. Through the lives of nine women writers, including George Eliot, Toni Morrison, and Sylvia Plath, this is a radical exploration of creativity, gender, and selfhood. Join Biggs as she speaks with writer Octavia Bright.

Title: Ghaith Abdul-Ahad & Gordon Corera: The Long Shadow of War
Teaser: Twenty years ago, the US-led ‘coalition of the willing’ invaded Iraq, leading to the downfall of Sadam Hussain’s government. In the UK, an estimated one million people joined the anti-war protest, questioning the legality and intentions of the...
Description: Twenty years ago, the US-led ‘coalition of the willing’ invaded Iraq, leading to the downfall of Sadam Hussain’s government. In the UK, an estimated one million people joined the anti-war protest, questioning the legality and intentions of the invasion. In A Stranger in Your Own City, Ghaith Abdul-Ahad tells the story of Baghdad civilians – a moving account of a place that, even after so long, remains dangerous for those demanding democracy. He's joined by the BBC security correspondent Gordon Corera, whose Radio 4 series Shock and War looks at the legacies of the invasion. Chaired by Allan Little.

Title: Anna Woltz & David Colmer: Woltzing Around the World with Tess
Teaser: Anna Woltz’s My Especially Weird Week with Tess, has been translated into 15 languages and awarded The Times Children’s Book of the Week. Hear about how the story's message of embracing the present moment in the face of an uncertain future still...
Description: Anna Woltz’s My Especially Weird Week with Tess, has been translated into 15 languages and awarded The Times Children’s Book of the Week. Hear about how the story's message of embracing the present moment in the face of an uncertain future still rings truer than ever with translator David Colmer. Discover adventure, friendship, and finding family in the places you least expect.

Title: The Missing Piece with Jordan Stephens & Beth Suzanna
Teaser: Small but determined, Sunny sets off on a whirlwind adventure of new places and friends, and discovers that looking for something is every bit as fun as finding it! Join writer and performer Jordan Stephens and illustrator Beth Suzanna for a...
Description: Small but determined, Sunny sets off on a whirlwind adventure of new places and friends, and discovers that looking for something is every bit as fun as finding it! Join writer and performer Jordan Stephens and illustrator Beth Suzanna for a heart-warming and exciting picture book event, celebrating the power of family bonds, the joy of making new friends and the importance of finding what makes you feel whole.

Title: David Olusoga: Black British History
Teaser: Join historian, author, and broadcaster David Olusoga, for a fascinating introduction to Black British history, with Waterstones Children’s Laureate Joseph Coelho. From the Roman Africans who guarded Hadrian’s Wall to the present day, David...
Description: Join historian, author, and broadcaster David Olusoga, for a fascinating introduction to Black British history, with Waterstones Children’s Laureate Joseph Coelho. From the Roman Africans who guarded Hadrian’s Wall to the present day, David highlights some key moments in Black British history from the past 1800 years and presents a sneak-peek of his new book, Black History for Every Day of the Year, written with his sister Yinka, which features both well-known figures and unsung heroes.

Title: Richard T Kelly: Scotland’s Black Gold Rush
Teaser: North Sea oil exploration has been a subject of impassioned debate in Scottish life, and literature. Writer Richard T Kelly makes it the subject of his evocative novel The Black Eden. Charting the promise of ‘black gold’, he spins a fascinating...
Description: North Sea oil exploration has been a subject of impassioned debate in Scottish life, and literature. Writer Richard T Kelly makes it the subject of his evocative novel The Black Eden. Charting the promise of ‘black gold’, he spins a fascinating story about five characters from different walks of life affected by the oil boom. Today, Kelly discusses his work with Mary Paulson-Ellis.

Title: Judith Schalansky: Maps of the Imagination
Teaser: In 2022, Judith Schalansky was named as the ninth author to write secret work for Future Library which will remain unpublished until 2114. With two genre-defying books, An Inventory of Losses and Atlas of Remote Islands, Schalansky has forged a special...
Description: In 2022, Judith Schalansky was named as the ninth author to write secret work for Future Library which will remain unpublished until 2114. With two genre-defying books, An Inventory of Losses and Atlas of Remote Islands, Schalansky has forged a special place as a poetic conjuror of things that can only exist in our imaginations. Whether they’re unreachable islands or Greta Garbo’s fading beauty, Schalansky’s creations are fearsomely evocative. In conversation with Cal Flyn.

Title: Shared Reading with Open Book
Teaser: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session over a hot drink in the Edinburgh College of Art Café. Each session includes different books from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading...
Description: Join Open Book Lead Readers for an informal and relaxed shared reading session over a hot drink in the Edinburgh College of Art Café. Each session includes different books from this year’s Festival programme. No experience necessary, all reading materials are provided on the day.

Title: Leonie Bell & Jonathan Faiers: Tartan – Textile of Royalty and Ruffians
Teaser: National icon; fashion statement; tool of colonialist power: tartan's origins are steeped in symbolism, and fraught with contradictions. As Scotland enjoys a major exhibition about tartan at V&A Dundee, the museum’s director Leonie Bell is joined by...
Description: National icon; fashion statement; tool of colonialist power: tartan's origins are steeped in symbolism, and fraught with contradictions. As Scotland enjoys a major exhibition about tartan at V&A Dundee, the museum’s director Leonie Bell is joined by consultant curator and fashion academic Jonathan Faiers to discuss the textile’s relationship to clanship, identity, and creativity, as well as tartan as a global phenomenon past and present. Chaired by Sally Magnusson. Get 20% off admission to Tartan at the V&A Dundee with tickets purchased to this event. Go to edbookfest.co.uk/terms-conditions/competition for full terms and conditions.

Title: Saving Neverland with Abi Elphinstone
Teaser: From Arctic dog-sledding to living with the Mongolian Kazakh eagle hunters, bestselling children’s author Abi Elphinstone shares the real-life adventures behind her epic stories. Hear Abi speaking about her latest book, Saving Neverland – a...
Description: From Arctic dog-sledding to living with the Mongolian Kazakh eagle hunters, bestselling children’s author Abi Elphinstone shares the real-life adventures behind her epic stories. Hear Abi speaking about her latest book, Saving Neverland – a modern, magical sequel to Peter Pan – complete with moonpaper maps, frostbears, and a woolly mammoth. She'll also be showing you just how easy it is to leap into stories of your own.

Title: Annie Macmanus: A Soundtrack for Orla
Teaser: Broadcaster, DJ, and Sunday Times bestselling author Annie Macmanus returns with The Mess We’re In. A love letter to the turn of the millennium, Macmanus’s second novel is a sharply realised coming-of-age tale as aspiring musician and Irish girl...
Description: Broadcaster, DJ, and Sunday Times bestselling author Annie Macmanus returns with The Mess We’re In. A love letter to the turn of the millennium, Macmanus’s second novel is a sharply realised coming-of-age tale as aspiring musician and Irish girl Orla arrives in London with her CD collection and little else. Join her today for a discussion about the power of music in forming identity and community. In conversation with Sinéad Gleeson.

Title: Self Portrait Masterclass with Pilar García de Leániz
Teaser: From Van Gogh to Picasso, artists have long been fascinated with self-portraits. In this special masterclass with illustrator and Edinburgh College of Art lecturer Pilar García de Leániz, learn the basic skills to create a self-portrait, then hone...
Description: From Van Gogh to Picasso, artists have long been fascinated with self-portraits. In this special masterclass with illustrator and Edinburgh College of Art lecturer Pilar García de Leániz, learn the basic skills to create a self-portrait, then hone your craft by creating an image of yourself to take home. Everyone is welcome from beginners to expert artists. Just remember – if Picasso drew his nose on his chin so can you!

Title: Jan Carson, Fergal Keane & Aoife Moore: After Good Friday
Teaser: How fragile is peace, even 25 years after the Good Friday Agreement? Three Irish writers discuss their perspectives. Jan Carson is a community arts worker and writer of The Raptures and east Belfast-set The Fire Starters; Fergal Keane was the BBC’s...
Description: How fragile is peace, even 25 years after the Good Friday Agreement? Three Irish writers discuss their perspectives. Jan Carson is a community arts worker and writer of The Raptures and east Belfast-set The Fire Starters; Fergal Keane was the BBC’s Northern Ireland correspondent during the Troubles and writes about the Irish war of Independence; and Irish Journalist of the Year 2021, Aoife Moore, explores the rise of Sinn Féin in her upcoming book The Long Game. Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Gerda Stevenson & J L Williams: To Care is Human
Teaser: Two poets reflect on the need for compassion in selfish times. Can words bring light to our ‘forlorn planet’? Tomorrow’s Feast by Gerda Stevenson draws on Scots, Gaelic, and English to create insightful, tender poems. Meanwhile, in Origin, J L...
Description: Two poets reflect on the need for compassion in selfish times. Can words bring light to our ‘forlorn planet’? Tomorrow’s Feast by Gerda Stevenson draws on Scots, Gaelic, and English to create insightful, tender poems. Meanwhile, in Origin, J L Williams explores the complexities of creating a new life in poems appealing to ‘all people who have entered through that small crack into the light of this life’. Chaired by Casi Dylan.

Title: Zaffar Kunial & Alice Oswald: Side by Side
Teaser: Two of Britain’s leading poets take to the stage to read new work that is being developed in parallel. Zaffar Kunial’s influential work includes the recent collection England’s Green. Alice Oswald’s work includes Memorial, the much-admired...
Description: Two of Britain’s leading poets take to the stage to read new work that is being developed in parallel. Zaffar Kunial’s influential work includes the recent collection England’s Green. Alice Oswald’s work includes Memorial, the much-admired reshaping of Homer’s Iliad. We are thrilled that in today’s session Kunial and Oswald are presenting yet-to-be-published work and poems in progress. Chaired by Marjorie Lotfi.

Title: Xiaolu Guo & Claudia Piñeiro: The Persistence of the Past
Teaser: Xiaolu Guo’s new memoir, Radical, explores what it’s like to exist as an outsider, separated from family and encountering a new culture, while Claudia Piñeiro's In A Little Luck explores the tragedies, big and small, that can ripple out from a...
Description: Xiaolu Guo’s new memoir, Radical, explores what it’s like to exist as an outsider, separated from family and encountering a new culture, while Claudia Piñeiro's In A Little Luck explores the tragedies, big and small, that can ripple out from a single decisive event. Join us to hear these two inspiring writers discuss the power of narrative, memory, and navigating the past. In conversation with Catherine Wilson.

Title: Elaine Feeney: Boy on a Mission
Teaser: Award-winning Irish novelist, performer, and playwright Elaine Feeney joins us to discuss her latest novel, How To Build A Boat. It’s the story of a 13 year old with big dreams and an even bigger imagination. Described by Douglas Stuart as ‘a...
Description:
Award-winning Irish novelist, performer, and playwright Elaine Feeney joins us to discuss her latest novel, How To Build A Boat. It’s the story of a 13 year old with big dreams and an even bigger imagination. Described by Douglas Stuart as ‘a gorgeous gift of a novel, hopeful and full of humanity’, it is being hailed as the most uplifting book of the year. Come along to find out why.

	In conversation with Sinéad Gleeson.

Title: The Bone Season: 10th Anniversary with Samantha Shannon
Teaser: Samantha Shannon was still a student when she published the first of her seven-book cycle The Bone Season set in a gothic vision of future London where humans with a capacity to contact the undead are persecuted for their abilities. This August sees the...
Description: Samantha Shannon was still a student when she published the first of her seven-book cycle The Bone Season set in a gothic vision of future London where humans with a capacity to contact the undead are persecuted for their abilities. This August sees the release of a new 10th anniversary edition of the international bestseller, boasting rewritten sections and bonus content. Samantha is in conversation with fellow author V. E Schwab to discuss what made it into this this ‘director’s cut’ of The Bone Season, her ground-breaking debut fantasy.

Title: Peter Ross: Places of Worship
Teaser: Across the UK, no building is quite as ubiquitous as the church. From Welsh holy wells to Britain's smallest parish church, Peter Ross journeys across the country to discover the history, art, and architecture contained under spires. Ross won 2021’s...
Description: Across the UK, no building is quite as ubiquitous as the church. From Welsh holy wells to Britain's smallest parish church, Peter Ross journeys across the country to discover the history, art, and architecture contained under spires. Ross won 2021’s Scotland’s National Book Award for A Tomb With A View, and his new book, Steeple Chasing, is another idiosyncratic and delightful travelogue of British history.  In conversation with Sheena McDonald.

Title: Amazing Bodies with Dr Ronx
Teaser: Join award-winning emergency doctor and TV presenter Dr Ronx as they take you on an interactive tour around the human body through their brilliant new book Amazing Bodies. From spongy brains to gooey guts and everything in between, Amazing...
Description: Join award-winning emergency doctor and TV presenter Dr Ronx as they take you on an interactive tour around the human body through their brilliant new book Amazing Bodies. From spongy brains to gooey guts and everything in between, Amazing Bodies is a fun introduction to human anatomy for budding experts and is packed with fascinating facts to wow all your friends. Chaired by Nick Sheridan.

Title: Building a Writing Career
Teaser: For many budding writers the idea of simply being published is enough but what happens next? How do you establish and develop a writing career that makes you a living? In this panel chaired by Heather Parry, four authors share the highs and lows of...
Description: For many budding writers the idea of simply being published is enough but what happens next? How do you establish and develop a writing career that makes you a living? In this panel chaired by Heather Parry, four authors share the highs and lows of their careers and explore how they developed the resilience and skills needed to sustain them financially and creatively. Featuring Helen Sedgwick, Jenny Colgan, Nadine Aisha Jassat, and Nikesh Shukla.

Title: Harry Baker & Courtney Stoddart: A Beginner's Guide to Performance Poetry
Teaser: One of literature’s hottest art forms, spoken word depends on great poetry and excellent performance skills. Join acclaimed poet and performer, Courtney Stoddart, and World Poetry Slam Champion, Harry Baker, in this workshop chaired by Nasim Rebecca...
Description: One of literature’s hottest art forms, spoken word depends on great poetry and excellent performance skills. Join acclaimed poet and performer, Courtney Stoddart, and World Poetry Slam Champion, Harry Baker, in this workshop chaired by Nasim Rebecca Asl. The session offers tips for developing your craft, advice on your rights as a performer and author, as well as exercises for honing your performance skills. This is a practical workshop open to any aspiring poetry performer and involves exercises in a group setting.

Title: Yomi Adegoke & Sheena Patel: Exploring Fiction’s Frontiers
Teaser: Today, we bring together Yomi Adegoke and Sheena Patel, two debut novelists who are forging new paths in contemporary fiction. In The List, Adegoke explores secrets, lies, and our online lives. Patel’s I’m A Fan grapples with toxic relationships,...
Description: Today, we bring together Yomi Adegoke and Sheena Patel, two debut novelists who are forging new paths in contemporary fiction. In The List, Adegoke explores secrets, lies, and our online lives. Patel’s I’m A Fan grapples with toxic relationships, social media, and patriarchal systems. Join us as they share their insights into what it’s like to write about contemporary life in all its complexity. Chaired by Tomiwa Folorunso.

Title: Debora Kayembe, David McCrone & David Pollock: Talk of the Town
Teaser: Every year, we celebrate the excitement and joy of Edinburgh’s festival season, yet the ‘Festival City’ has not been without its critics. Join arts writer David Pollock, author of The Edinburgh Festival: A Biography, leading sociologist David...
Description: Every year, we celebrate the excitement and joy of Edinburgh’s festival season, yet the ‘Festival City’ has not been without its critics. Join arts writer David Pollock, author of The Edinburgh Festival: A Biography, leading sociologist David McCrone, author of Who Runs Edinburgh?, and Debora Kayembe, rector at The University of Edinburgh, for a fascinating discussion on the forces shaping the city's cultural power and status. Chaired by Catherine Salmond.

Title: Anna Keay: Long Live The Republic
Teaser: Between Charles I’s execution and Charles II’s restoration, 17th century Britain saw the possibilities of a republic and the challenges of a conservative people trying to create one. Moving the spotlight from Oliver Cromwell to a cast of nine...
Description: Between Charles I’s execution and Charles II’s restoration, 17th century Britain saw the possibilities of a republic and the challenges of a conservative people trying to create one. Moving the spotlight from Oliver Cromwell to a cast of nine figures who made names for themselves during The Interregnum, Anna Keay’s brilliant account, The Restless Republic, illuminates the most revolutionary and experimental period in Britain’s political history. In conversation with Stuart Kelly.

Title: Take an Inspiring Slow Walk with Carl Honoré
Teaser: In a world addicted to speed, slowness is a superpower. On this walking tour, take time to connect with the world on a slow adventure around the surrounds of Edinburgh College of Art with Carl Honoré, the voice of the global Slow Movement. In his book,...
Description: In a world addicted to speed, slowness is a superpower. On this walking tour, take time to connect with the world on a slow adventure around the surrounds of Edinburgh College of Art with Carl Honoré, the voice of the global Slow Movement. In his book, It’s the Journey Not the Destination, Carl shows how young people can slow down, notice, and enjoy the things around them to thrive in an impatient world. Meet at the Box Office.
