Join Vivian French and Lucy Juckes, the founders of Picture Hooks, to discuss recently published picture books and classic favourites. They will be joined by expert colleagues to showcase the very best picture books for everyone from 0 to 99 years old.

Title: Victory to Words: A Celebration of Salman Rushdie
Teaser: The publication of Victory City, Salman Rushdie’s fifteenth novel, is a beautiful reminder of the author’s scintillating imagination. An exuberant story brimming with humour, this is Rushdie’s finest novel in years. Written before the attack on...
Description: The publication of Victory City, Salman Rushdie’s fifteenth novel, is a beautiful reminder of the author’s scintillating imagination. An exuberant story brimming with humour, this is Rushdie’s finest novel in years. Written before the attack on the author last year, this novel turns out not only to be a rollicking read but also an act of defiance. Today, admirers of his work Chitra Ramaswamy, Simon Schama, and Nicola Sturgeon discuss the novels that have changed and shaped their lives. Chaired by Nick Barley.

Title: Gavin Francis & Devi Sridhar: The Cost of Health
Teaser: The result of a pandemic and an ageing UK population: record waiting times for treatment. Conversely, medical advances are saving and prolonging lives – albeit ever more expensively. If the NHS is broken, how can we afford the cure? Writer and GP...
Description: The result of a pandemic and an ageing UK population: record waiting times for treatment. Conversely, medical advances are saving and prolonging lives – albeit ever more expensively. If the NHS is broken, how can we afford the cure? Writer and GP Gavin Francis, author of Free For All: Why The NHS Is Worth Saving, presents a passionate defence of NHS principles, while global public health expert Devi Sridhar offers an international perspective. Chaired by Peter Mathieson, vice chancellor of the University of Edinburgh.

Title: Scribble, Scrawl and Crawl Walking Tour with Jill Calder and Justin Davies
Teaser: Be inspired by the sights and sounds in and around the Book Festival and flex your creative muscles on a drawing and writing workshop with amazing award-winning duo, illustrator Jill Calder and children’s author Justin Davies, and hosted by SCBWI...
Description: Be inspired by the sights and sounds in and around the Book Festival and flex your creative muscles on a drawing and writing workshop with amazing award-winning duo, illustrator Jill Calder and children’s author Justin Davies, and hosted by SCBWI Scotland network organisers Lynwen Pirie and Caroline Deacon. This fun and informal walking tour is perfect for budding young illustrators and writers. Please dress appropriately for outdoor weather conditions. Meet at the Box Office to start the tour.

Title: Sprog Rock are in the House
Teaser: Back to rock the Book Festival for the third year, it’s Sprog Rock! This year the band will include Glasgow-based beatboxer Bigg Taj, so expect beats and (nursery) rhymes as Sprog Rock bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Courtyard Stage. Fun...
Description: Back to rock the Book Festival for the third year, it’s Sprog Rock! This year the band will include Glasgow-based beatboxer Bigg Taj, so expect beats and (nursery) rhymes as Sprog Rock bring their unique, catchy songs back to our Courtyard Stage. Fun for under-fives, their grown-ups, friends, and families.

Title: Tell Me About… Science! With Emily Dodd
Teaser: Explore the world around you and the world inside you in this interactive event based on the exciting new science series for young learners, Tell Me About…, by author (and science geek!) Emily Dodd. Discover how bees help plants and how plants help...
Description: Explore the world around you and the world inside you in this interactive event based on the exciting new science series for young learners, Tell Me About…, by author (and science geek!) Emily Dodd. Discover how bees help plants and how plants help us. Hear more about some of the weird and wonderful plants we have. And even find out how feelings are different for everyone and what makes your heart beat.

Title: Illustrator Surgery with the Bright Agency
Teaser:
Calling all children's book illustrators!  Now is your opportunity to have your work seen by a professional illustration agent.
Join The Bright Agency's Susan Penny for a unique portfolio review where she gives you handy pointers and advice as you make...
Description: Calling all children's book illustrators! Now is your opportunity to have your work seen by a professional illustration agent. Join The Bright Agency's Susan Penny for a unique portfolio review where she gives you handy pointers and advice as you make the next step in your career. Book your free 10 minute slot by calling the Box Office on 0345 373 5888. Tickets go on sale 29 June.

Title: Thomas Morris: The Short of It
Teaser: Thomas Morris is the editor-at-large of the Stinging Fly – the small publication with an enormous cultural output. He is also an accomplished, strikingly original writer, with an award-winning debut collection of short stories, We Don’t Know What...
Description: Thomas Morris is the editor-at-large of the Stinging Fly – the small publication with an enormous cultural output. He is also an accomplished, strikingly original writer, with an award-winning debut collection of short stories, We Don’t Know What We're Doing, and the dazzling follow up, Open Up. Join Morris for a conversation about his original collection and the specific craft of the short story. In conversation with Oliver Mol.

Title: Lizzy Stewart: Illustrated Reading Lists
Teaser: Many people keep a list of the books they've read – but why not make it an illustrated list? Choose your four favourite books of the year and bring pictures of their covers to this practical session with illustrator and graphic novelist Lizzy Stewart....
Description: Many people keep a list of the books they've read – but why not make it an illustrated list? Choose your four favourite books of the year and bring pictures of their covers to this practical session with illustrator and graphic novelist Lizzy Stewart. She helps you turn them into a gorgeous illustration – and leaves you with the tools to keep an illustrated record of your books of the year. Stewart is the author of several books including her most recent graphic novel Alison.

Title: Lizzy Stewart: Introduction to Graphic Storytelling
Teaser: Join graphic novelist and artist Lizzy Stewart – author of Alison and Walking Distance – as she guides you through a series of creative techniques for graphic novels. Sharing her insights into her own illustrative process, Stewart will demonstrate...
Description: Join graphic novelist and artist Lizzy Stewart – author of Alison and Walking Distance – as she guides you through a series of creative techniques for graphic novels. Sharing her insights into her own illustrative process, Stewart will demonstrate how to get started or continue with your visual storytelling.

Title: Sunday Salon: Maria Fusco & Margaret Salmon
Teaser: Northern Irish writer Maria Fusco, British-American artist filmmaker Margaret Salmon, and composer Annea Lockwood have collaborated on History of the Present, a hybrid opera that will be performed live at Edinburgh Art Festival. In the first of our...
Description: Northern Irish writer Maria Fusco, British-American artist filmmaker Margaret Salmon, and composer Annea Lockwood have collaborated on History of the Present, a hybrid opera that will be performed live at Edinburgh Art Festival. In the first of our Sunday Salon series, join Fusco and Salmon as they speak to Kim McAleese, Director of Edinburgh Art Festival, about their work that foregrounds working class women’s voices. This salon is presented in partnership with the Edinburgh Art Festival and the Edinburgh International Film Festival.

Title: The Edinburgh ReaderBank: An Experiment in Imagination
Teaser: What happens – in our minds and brains, hearts and relationships – when we read? In 2023 the Festival has partnered with Durham University to design the world’s most ambitious study of reading, imagination, and health – and we want your input....
Description: What happens – in our minds and brains, hearts and relationships – when we read? In 2023 the Festival has partnered with Durham University to design the world’s most ambitious study of reading, imagination, and health – and we want your input. Join the team behind the project for a lively introduction to the ideas animating existing research and information on how to be involved.

Title: Close Read: Marion Turner on Refugee Tales
Teaser: Take a deep dive into the first volume of Refugee Tales, the product of a collaboration between authors and refugee charity the Gatwick Detainees Welfare Group, which sends volunteers to speak to the hundreds of people held at the airport’s detention...
Description: Take a deep dive into the first volume of Refugee Tales, the product of a collaboration between authors and refugee charity the Gatwick Detainees Welfare Group, which sends volunteers to speak to the hundreds of people held at the airport’s detention centres. Marion Turner, Chaucer biographer and author of The Wife of Bath, guides readers through this modern-day Canterbury Tales. This workshop is suitable for those with existing knowledge of Refugee Tales and for those new to this work.

Title: Close Read: Sarah Krasnostein on Narrative Non-Fiction
Teaser: Writers of narrative non-fiction need as much information as possible to tell true stories both accurately and creatively. Having too little access – or too much information – can feel daunting. In this workshop, join The Trauma Cleaner writer and...
Description: Writers of narrative non-fiction need as much information as possible to tell true stories both accurately and creatively. Having too little access – or too much information – can feel daunting. In this workshop, join The Trauma Cleaner writer and critic Sarah Krasnostein to discuss how to clear those hurdles in texts by John Berger, Emmanuel Carrère, Rachel Kaadzi Ghansah, Janet Malcom, and Gay Talese. Enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of these writers and for those new to their work.

Title: Close Read: Jess Brough on Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments
Teaser: Take a deep dive into Saidiya Hartman's Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments with writer and Fringe of Colour founder Jess Brough. Join for an illuminating discussion of Hartman’s expert scholarship around life for Black women in the wake of...
Description: Take a deep dive into Saidiya Hartman's Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments with writer and Fringe of Colour founder Jess Brough. Join for an illuminating discussion of Hartman’s expert scholarship around life for Black women in the wake of emancipation from slavery and their courageous experiments with real freedom, to shape family life and love outside of straight and conventional norms. Enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments and for those new to Hartman's work.

Title: Liner Notes: Amy Key on Joni Mitchell
Teaser: Today, join poet, writer, and author of Arrangements in Blue: Notes on Love and Making a Life, Amy Key, for a close listen of the woman whose work underpins Key’s memoir: legendary musician, producer and songwriter Joni Mitchell. Celebrate one of the...
Description: Today, join poet, writer, and author of Arrangements in Blue: Notes on Love and Making a Life, Amy Key, for a close listen of the woman whose work underpins Key’s memoir: legendary musician, producer and songwriter Joni Mitchell. Celebrate one of the world’s best known and most loved lyricists in this workshop: an enjoyable audible adventure for those with deep knowledge of Mitchell’s work, and for newcomers.

Title: Jan Carson: Why Your Writing is Broken and How to Fix It
Teaser: Join writer Jan Carson for this interactive workshop focusing on the mistakes almost every writer makes and how to avoid making them in your own writing. Take this opportunity to identify areas where you could significantly improve your creative...
Description: Join writer Jan Carson for this interactive workshop focusing on the mistakes almost every writer makes and how to avoid making them in your own writing. Take this opportunity to identify areas where you could significantly improve your creative process, and to explore where your writing’s going wrong on a sentence by sentence basis. All participants should come with a working draft they’re keen to edit. The workshop is particularly aimed at novelists and short story writers though it will contain useful advice for everyone.

Title: Close Read: Sophie Cunningham on M John Harrison
Teaser: Take a deep dive into the spectacular world of M John Harrison and his 2020 Goldsmith Prize winning novel, The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again, with Sophie Cunningham, author of the playfully haunted This Devastating Fever. Hear how fragmented reality,...
Description: Take a deep dive into the spectacular world of M John Harrison and his 2020 Goldsmith Prize winning novel, The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again, with Sophie Cunningham, author of the playfully haunted This Devastating Fever. Hear how fragmented reality, a love story, and political takeovers combine in this ‘realist fantasy’. This 90-minute workshop will be enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again and for those new to Harrison's work.

Title: Happy High Status: Masterclass with Viv Groskop
Teaser: Is there a way to move effortlessly through life? Perhaps not completely, but you can certainly get a lot closer to it today. Part talk, part workshop, this is a cringe-free masterclass on confidence and presence with comedian and bestselling author Viv...
Description: Is there a way to move effortlessly through life? Perhaps not completely, but you can certainly get a lot closer to it today. Part talk, part workshop, this is a cringe-free masterclass on confidence and presence with comedian and bestselling author Viv Groskop, based on her new book Happy High Status. Groskop is also the host of the chart-topping podcast How to Own the Room, and her work is ‘recommended to anyone wanting more self-confidence’ by psychotherapist Philippa Perry.

Title: Close Read with Eileen Myles
Teaser: Eileen Myles is a poet, performer, and activist whose work spans poetry, short stories, creative non-fiction, performance pieces, and even a run for president. Their writing often crosses from the universe at large to more intimate concerns, interested...
Description: Poet, performer and activist Eileen Myles is inextricably linked to New York City but join them today as they explore the world of 17th century England in Victor Hugo’s novel, The Man Who Laughs. Like much of Hugo’s work, this story is preoccupied with violence and hypocrisy in the aristocracy, and the lonely figures who can be both victims and heroes. This 90-minute workshop will be enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of The Man Who Laughs and for those new to Hugo’s work.

Title: Jan Carson: The Short Story Writer's Starter Kit
Teaser: Interested in writing short stories? Struggling to know where to start? This interactive course facilitated by writer Jan Carson guides you through the basics of writing imaginative and engaging short stories. The two and a half hour session focuses...
Description: Interested in writing short stories? Struggling to know where to start? This interactive course facilitated by writer Jan Carson guides you through the basics of writing imaginative and engaging short stories. The two and a half hour session focuses upon key themes such as developing ideas, writing believable characters and convincing dialogue, plot, and structure. This workshop is suitable for beginning writers. All you need is a notebook, a pen, and a fully functioning imagination.

Title: Close Read with Guy Gunaratne
Teaser: Guy Gunaratne is a journalist, documentary film-maker, and novelist whose debut work, In Our Mad and Furious City, was shortlisted for the Booker Prize. They return to the Festival this year with their second novel, Mister, Mister, which focuses on what...
Description: Only recently available to the general public, Through the Billboard Promised Land Without Ever Stopping is Derek Jarman’s only novel, and today Guy Gunaratne, author of Mister, Mister, will be providing an in-depth analysis of this work. The surrealist story follows a blind man called King and his valet on a trip across an imagined America, encountering characters along the way. If you love Jarman’s work as an artist, a writer, and a filmmaker, come and be introduced to this mini masterpiece of narrative fiction.

Title: Liner Notes: Michel Faber on Krautrock
Teaser: Today, join novelist and author of soon-to-be-published Listen: On Music, Sound and Us Michel Faber for a musical journey far beyond the borders of Anglo rock. This 90-minute workshop, suitable for any curious listener, will explore the sounds, origins,...
Description: Today, join novelist and author of soon-to-be-published Listen: On Music, Sound and Us Michel Faber for a musical journey far beyond the borders of Anglo rock. This 90-minute workshop, suitable for any curious listener, will explore the sounds, origins, and echoes of Krautrock, Germany's influential but misunderstood post-war musical miracle. The autobahn will take us deep into the forest and to outer space.

Title: Close Read: Rodge Glass on Some Rain Must Fall
Teaser: Take a deep dive into Michel Faber's dazzling and versatile short story collection Some Rain Must Fall and Other Stories, and celebrate its 25th anniversary with Rodge Glass, writer, Senior Lecturer in Creative Writing at University of Strathclyde and...
Description: Take a deep dive into Michel Faber's dazzling and versatile short story collection Some Rain Must Fall and Other Stories, and celebrate its 25th anniversary with Rodge Glass, writer, Senior Lecturer in Creative Writing at University of Strathclyde and author of newly released Michel Faber: The Writer and His Work. This 90-minute workshop will be enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of Some Rain Must Fall and for those new to Faber’s work.

Title: Kezia Dugdale & Lesley Riddoch: Once Upon a Time in Holyrood
Teaser: When Humza Yousaf became the sixth First Minister of Scotland, he promised, "new leadership, a fresh start for Scotland" – but amid the enquiries and intrigue, what does that really mean? Join our panel including former Leader of Scottish Labour,...
Description:
When Humza Yousaf became the sixth First Minister of Scotland, he promised, "new leadership, a fresh start for Scotland" – but amid the enquiries and intrigue, what does that really mean? Join our panel including former Leader of Scottish Labour, Kezia Dugdale and broadcaster and journalist Lesley Riddoch as they take us through the turbulences and triumphs of modern Scottish politics, and ultimately ask: what next for Scotland?

	Chaired by Ruth Wishart.

Title: Amina Cain: Words to Live By
Teaser: When it comes to fiction, we often think first and foremost about plot and narrative; in other words, the larger picture. But what happens when we turn our attention more fully to detail, as a painter might, across which narrative might also unfold?...
Description: When it comes to fiction, we often think first and foremost about plot and narrative; in other words, the larger picture. But what happens when we turn our attention more fully to detail, as a painter might, across which narrative might also unfold? Working from the idea that one or two striking details is worth more than an entire paragraph of general description, join writer Amina Cain to look at how we might engage with this element of fiction in a rich and expressive way.

Title: Nikesh Shukla: Writing With Intent
Teaser: Nikesh Shukla, author, writing mentor, and bestselling editor of The Good Immigrant, knows better than most the power that every unique voice has to create change. Whether it's a novel, personal essay, non-fiction work, or short story – or even just...
Description: Nikesh Shukla, author, writing mentor, and bestselling editor of The Good Immigrant, knows better than most the power that every unique voice has to create change. Whether it's a novel, personal essay, non-fiction work, or short story – or even just the formless desire to write something – this workshop will help you to set your intentions for your writing, help you to balance storytelling instinct with structure, and build your characters.

Title: Susannah Dickey: Dialogue in Fiction
Teaser: Join novelist and poet Susannah Dickey for a fascinating two and a half hour session on the power of dialogue in fiction. With samples taken from a broad span of global contemporary fiction, in this workshop you will study ways of providing exposition...
Description: Join novelist and poet Susannah Dickey for a fascinating two and a half hour session on the power of dialogue in fiction. With samples taken from a broad span of global contemporary fiction, in this workshop you will study ways of providing exposition through dialogue in nuanced and subtle ways; learn how to make your characters distinctive through their speaking styles; and study how humour in dialogue can supplement and strengthen tragic or serious topics.

Title: Dan Richards: Non-Fiction Masterclass
Teaser: Sunday Times Bestselling author Dan Richards returns to Book Festival for a masterclass exploring different approaches to writing adventurous non-fiction. This class covers narrative, voice, the importance of engaging directly and poetically with source...
Description: Sunday Times Bestselling author Dan Richards returns to Book Festival for a masterclass exploring different approaches to writing adventurous non-fiction. This class covers narrative, voice, the importance of engaging directly and poetically with source material, forms of research, the need to embracing accidents, and the power of asking simple child-like questions.

Title: Liner Notes: Leah Broad on Contemporary Classical Music
Teaser: Today, join University of Oxford music historian, and author of Quartet: How Four Women Changed the Musical World, Leah Broad for a close listen of contemporary classical music. This exciting range of work includes concertos, sonatas, and symphonies by...
Description: Today, join University of Oxford music historian, and author of Quartet: How Four Women Changed the Musical World, Leah Broad for a close listen of contemporary classical music. This exciting range of work includes concertos, sonatas, and symphonies by Rebecca Clarke, Jean Sibelius, Dobrinka Tabakova and Shelley Washington. An enjoyable audible adventure for those with a deep knowledge of these composers, and complete newcomers.

Title: Close Read: Daniel Hahn on International Booker Prize Winner
Teaser: As a shortlisted translator himself as well as a former judge, Daniel Hahn has seen both sides of the world of the International Booker Prize. With so much experience both as a reader and as a writer, he certainly knows how to spot the qualities that...
Description: As a shortlisted translator himself as well as a former judge, Daniel Hahn has seen both sides of the world of the International Booker Prize. With so much experience both as a reader and as a writer, he certainly knows how to spot the qualities that make a literary prize-winner. Join him today for a constructively-critical dive into this year's International Booker Prize winner, Time Shelter by Georgi Gospodinov and his translator Angela Rodel.

Title: Cal Flyn: Long Form Journalism
Teaser: Join the Scottish journalist and award-winning author of Islands of Abandonment Cal Flyn for a workshop in the art of long-form journalism, from pitch to publication. Discuss research methods, reporting, and the faithful reconstruction of events, before...
Description: Join the Scottish journalist and award-winning author of Islands of Abandonment Cal Flyn for a workshop in the art of long-form journalism, from pitch to publication. Discuss research methods, reporting, and the faithful reconstruction of events, before studying the narrative skills that allow us to tell nonfiction stories with novelistic flair - taking inspiration from star writers of publications including the New Yorker, the Guardian, and Granta.

Title: Jon Gray & Rafaela Romaya: Bookshelf Envy
Teaser: Between a writer and their reader is the book cover and its designer. They must imagine what will shine on the shelf, and convey a  book's spirit. In today’s workshop, join Jon Gray - alias gray318 - the cover designer for Zadie Smith, Sally Rooney,...
Description: Between a writer and their reader is the book cover and its designer. They must imagine what will shine on the shelf, and convey a  book's spirit. In today’s workshop, join Jon Gray - alias gray318 - the cover designer for Zadie Smith, Sally Rooney, and many others, and Canongate Art Director Rafaela Romaya, who has produced covers for the likes of Matt Haig and Michel Faber, as they reveal the work behind the designs, and give you the tools to create your own.

Title: Scottish BPOC Writers Network: Ghosts, Nanas and the Apocalypse
Teaser: How do our favourite authors connect with the stories of ancestors? In this special event, presented with Scottish BPOC Writers Network, join Rachelle Atalla, Lorraine Wilson, Nadine Aisha Jassat, and Tendai Huchu as they share what reaching out to...
Description: How do our favourite authors connect with the stories of ancestors? In this special event, presented with Scottish BPOC Writers Network, join Rachelle Atalla, Lorraine Wilson, Nadine Aisha Jassat, and Tendai Huchu as they share what reaching out to ancestors and descendants looks like and let us in on some of the secrets of calling upon the past to inspire future stories. Chaired by Courtney Stoddart.

Title: Stella Chan & Alison Harper: Understanding Mental Health
Teaser: There has been an alarming increase in mental health issues amongst young people. Mental health – especially youth depression – remains a difficult topic, clouded by misconceptions. In this informative event, experts Professor Stella Chan and Dr...
Description: There has been an alarming increase in mental health issues amongst young people. Mental health – especially youth depression – remains a difficult topic, clouded by misconceptions. In this informative event, experts Professor Stella Chan and Dr Alison Harper, clinical psychologists specialising in adolescent health, consider how to best support young people’s well-being, drawing on the words and writing of a teenager who lost her life to suicide. Chaired by Claire Urquhart.

Title: Eileen Myles: 'They' Contain Multitudes
Teaser: Prolific poet and activist Eileen Myles is back with a “Working Life”, a new collection which captures the many dualities of human life: loneliness and companionship, travel and stasis, fear and wonder. Join us to hear Myles discuss the immense...
Description:
Prolific poet and activist Eileen Myles is back with a “Working Life”, a new collection which captures the many dualities of human life: loneliness and companionship, travel and stasis, fear and wonder. Join us to hear Myles discuss the immense anxieties about the future world, as well as the beauty to be found in landscapes, animals, and the act of caring for each other.

	In conversation with Harry Josephine Giles.

Title: M John Harrison: This Is Not a Memoir
Teaser: It would take some doing to rival M John Harrison’s genre-defying literary output. Each work – including 2020 Goldsmith Prize-winner The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again – has a rebelliousness of spirit that continues with Wish I Was Here: An...
Description: It would take some doing to rival M John Harrison’s genre-defying literary output. Each work – including 2020 Goldsmith Prize-winner The Sunken Land Begins to Rise Again – has a rebelliousness of spirit that continues with Wish I Was Here: An Anti-Memoir. Dedicated to ‘everyone who couldn’t think what to say’, this is a work about craft and the self from one of literature's most thrilling voices. In conversation with Samuel Fisher.

Title: Christie Watson: Wild At Heart
Teaser: Are we finally getting better at talking about middle age? A shining light leading us along is Christie Watson, writer of Quilt on Fire. Today she talks with broadcaster Sam Baker about the joys (plenty) and agonies (there are a few) of our middle years...
Description: Are we finally getting better at talking about middle age? A shining light leading us along is Christie Watson, writer of Quilt on Fire. Today she talks with broadcaster Sam Baker about the joys (plenty) and agonies (there are a few) of our middle years and everything that comes with being a woman with a wild heart, a changing body, and a new set of challenges.

Title: 2023 International Booker Prize Winners: Georgi Gospodinov & Angela Rodel
Teaser: The International Booker is the annual award for the best work of fiction translated into English from another language. With an equal prize to both author and translator, this is the most important prize for translated fiction. The shortlist comprised...

Title: Close Read: Open Book on Victoria Adukwei Bulley and Nina Mingya Powles
Teaser: Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity which organises shared reading and creative writing groups, explore brand new poetry collections: Quiet by Victoria Adukwei Bulley and Magnolia by Nina Mingya Powles. Join them for a close...
Description: Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity which organises shared reading and creative writing groups, explore brand new poetry collections: Quiet by Victoria Adukwei Bulley and Magnolia by Nina Mingya Powles. Join them for a close read of these exciting debuts. Expect an open discussion from the start – there is no preparation required.

Title: Black History Walking Tour with Lisa Williams
Teaser: Join the founder of the Edinburgh Caribbean Association, Lisa Williams, on a Black history walking tour of Edinburgh. With stops throughout the city to examine its architectural heritage, Williams illuminates the role of Scots in slavery and colonialism...
Description: Join the founder of the Edinburgh Caribbean Association, Lisa Williams, on a Black history walking tour of Edinburgh. With stops throughout the city to examine its architectural heritage, Williams illuminates the role of Scots in slavery and colonialism from a Caribbean perspective. She shares stories of Black people with heritage across the globe who visited and lived in Edinburgh, their ongoing influence on the city, and remarkable legacies. Meet at the Box Office to start the Tour.

Title: Centre for Open Learning: Creative Writing Workshop
Teaser: The Book Festival is delighted to be partnering with the Centre for Open Learning (COL) at the University of Edinburgh. Today, experienced teaching staff from COL's popular Creative Writing Short Courses will present a special Book Festival workshop,...
Description: The Book Festival is delighted to be partnering with the Centre for Open Learning (COL) at the University of Edinburgh. Today, experienced teaching staff from COL's popular Creative Writing Short Courses will present a special Book Festival workshop, guiding participants to explore their creativity in an accessible and supportive environment. Check edbookfest.co.uk for further details.

Title: Sunday Salon: Ira Sachs, Brandon Taylor and Kate Taylor
Teaser: Ira Sachs is in Edinburgh to present his latest film Passages, a daring, nuanced love-lust triangle that explores how narcissism can feed into creativity even as it causes relationships to implode. Join Sachs alongside Brandon Taylor – cultural...

Title: Close Read: Open Book on Girl, Woman, Other
Teaser: Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity which organises shared reading and creative writing groups, explore Girl Woman Other, Bernardine Evaristo’s delightfully inventive, and Booker Prize winning, 2019 work. Overlapping stories...
Description: Marjorie Lotfi and Claire Urquhart from Open Book, a charity which organises shared reading and creative writing groups, explore Girl, Woman, Other, Bernardine Evaristo’s delightfully inventive, and Booker Prize winning, 2019 work. Overlapping stories paint a picture of a joyful and complicated Black British experience, told in a poetic style. Expect an open discussion from the start – there is no preparation required.

Title: Close Read: Yara Rodrigues Fowler on Mansfield Park
Teaser: Take a deep dive into the conventions of Regency society, helped along by a writer who knew how to shoot a sly critique at the ridiculousness of its workings - it could only be Jane Austen. Novelist and activist Yara Rodrigues Fowler will guide you...
Description: Take a deep dive into the conventions of Regency society, helped along by a writer who knew how to shoot a sly critique at the ridiculousness of its workings - it could only be Jane Austen. Novelist and activist Yara Rodrigues Fowler will guide you through Austen’s – marginally – lesser-known novel, Mansfield Park and the complicated relations surrounding her quiet heroine, Fanny Brice. This workshop will be enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of Mansfield Park and for those new to Austen’s work.

Title: Close Read: Elaine Feeney on A Manual for Cleaning Women
Teaser: Today, join Irish poet, novelist, and playwright Elaine Feeney for an in-depth consideration of A Manual for Cleaning Women by Lucia Berlin. Many readers were unaware of Berlin when this collection of short stories appeared nearly a decade after the...
Description: Today, join Irish poet, novelist, and playwright Elaine Feeney for an in-depth consideration of A Manual for Cleaning Women by Lucia Berlin. Many readers were unaware of Berlin when this collection of short stories appeared nearly a decade after the writer’s death, but now her unsentimental, clear-eyed stories enjoy a popular position in the literary landscape. This 90-minute workshop will be enjoyable for those with existing knowledge of A Manual for Cleaning Women and for those new to Berlin’s work.

Title: Inside Out: Hiking
Teaser: Following on from our event Merryn Glover & Rachel Hewitt: Women in the Wild on 12 Aug, join the authors, along with endurance cyclist Emily Chappell for a hike through Edinburgh. 16 places available. Meet at the Box Office. This event will start from...

Title: Think Tank: Paul Johnson with Anton Muscatelli - Are We Getting Tax Policy Wrong?
Teaser: The British state raises – and spends – a whopping £1 trillion of taxpayers money each year. How that money is spent can determine the welfare of the poor and the elderly, the state of the health service, the effectiveness of our children's...
Description: The British state raises – and spends – a whopping £1 trillion of taxpayers money each year. How that money is spent can determine the welfare of the poor and the elderly, the state of the health service, the effectiveness of our children's education. How can we hold governments to account, improve the effectiveness of the tax system, and get a better outcome from that £1 trillion of spending? Join this Think Tank event with Paul Johnson, director of the highly influential Institute for Fiscal Studies, in conversation with Anton Muscatelli, Principal & Vice-Chancellor of the University of Glasgow and leading economist, as part of a special series encouraging deep discussion over food and drink.

Title: Inside Out: Cycling
Teaser:
Following on from our event Jenny Graham & Kate Rawles: A Better World On Two Wheels on 19 Aug, join the authors, along with endurance cyclist Emily Chappell, for a cycle in Edinburgh. 32 places available.

The cycle is at a sociable pace, and should...
Description:
Following on from our event Jenny Graham & Kate Rawles: A Better World On Two Wheels on 19 Aug, join the authors, along with endurance cyclist Emily Chappell, for a cycle in Edinburgh. 32 places available.
	 

	Set out from Gamma Transport Division in Stockbridge (a 7-minute ride from the Festival site), and the sociably paced road ride will last about 90 minutes, before heading back to the meeting place for coffee and snacks. All bikes (and riders) are welcome.

	This activity is at a sociable pace, and should be suitable for anyone who cycles regularly. There will be community ride leaders present to navigate the group, but participants must take responsibility for their own safety, dress appropriately for the weather, and carry the basic tools required to fix a puncture.

Title: Inside Out: Running
Teaser: In advance of our event Richard Askwith & Sabrina Pace-Humphreys: Running For Their Lives later today, join the authors, along with endurance cyclist Emily Chappell, for a run in Edinburgh. 24 places available.  The run is at a sociable pace, and should...

Title: Think Tank: Kate Crawford - How Can We Take Back Control of AI?
Teaser: There are plenty of caustic predictions about the threats to humanity posed by Artificial Intelligence. Leading scholar Kate Crawford has written a powerful new book, Atlas of AI, described by Science as 'a timely and urgent contribution,' demonstrating...
Description: There are plenty of caustic predictions about the threats to humanity posed by Artificial Intelligence. Leading scholar Kate Crawford has written a powerful new book, Atlas of AI, described by Science as 'a timely and urgent contribution,' demonstrating that the new infrastructures of AI serve the interests of the few at the expense of the many. How can we change that? Join this Think Tank event with Kate Crawford as part of a special series encouraging deep discussion accompanied by food and drink, in conversation with Allison Gardner.

Title: Think Tank: Jolyon Maugham KC – How Politics Went to War with the Law
Teaser: To what extent does – or should – politics intersect with the law? While the separation of the court from government is a tentpole principle of democracy, are there situations where they should mix, and to what end? Join us for this Think Tank event...
Description: To what extent does – or should – politics intersect with the law? While the separation of the court from government is a tentpole principle of democracy, are there situations where they should mix, and to what end? Join us for this Think Tank event with Jolyon Maugham KC, the executive director of the Good Law Project, a special series that encourages discussion between the audience accompanied by food and drink. Chaired by Aamer Anwara.

Title: Kate Crawford: Who Wins in the AI Revolution?
Teaser: Artificial intelligence and the advent of programmes like ChatGPT are dominating the news. Join us to hear academic and senior Microsoft researcher Kate Crawford, one of the world’s leading scholars of the social and political implications of AI,...
Description: Artificial intelligence and the advent of programmes like ChatGPT are dominating the news. Join us to hear academic and senior Microsoft researcher Kate Crawford, one of the world’s leading scholars of the social and political implications of AI, discuss Atlas of AI where she argues that the global networks underpinning AI technology are damaging the environment, entrenching inequality, and fueling a shift toward undemocratic governance. In conversation with Chris Speed.

Title: Close Read with Joanna Biggs
Teaser: Joanna Biggs is a writer and senior editor at Harper's Magazine. In her deeply moving, A Life of One’s Own, the lives of nine women writers are brought to light and interwoven with Biggs’ own experiences. She questions themes of conventional...
Description: Joanna Biggs is a writer and senior editor at Harper's Magazine. In her deeply moving, A Life of One’s Own, the lives of nine women writers are brought to light and interwoven with Biggs’ own experiences. She questions themes of conventional domesticity, love and womanhood. In this workshop, it is only fitting that Biggs takes a deep dive into Norman Rush's Mating, set in an experimental women-only utopia, an intelligent female lead, and questions over societal norms. Join Biggs for this 90-minute workshop, enjoyable for those familiar with Mating and those new to Rush's work.

Title: Judy Murray: The Wild Card
Teaser: JJudy Murray's dedication to tennis is recognised internationally with her extensive tennis and coaching achievements to date. Today, she talks about her debut novel, The Wild Card. Set at a tennis tournament, it centres on a 38 year old woman...
Description: Judy Murray's dedication to tennis is recognised internationally with her extensive tennis and coaching achievements to date. Today, she talks about her debut novel, The Wild Card. Set at a tennis tournament, it centres on a 38 year old woman successfully rekindling her playing career, years after putting it on hold. But the threat of her secret looms… Murray discusses her tale of triumph over adversity. In conversation with Nicola Meighan.

Description:
Caleb Azumah Nelson is a photographer and the writer of Small Worlds and the award-winning Open Water. In the latter, the unnamed narrator notes, ‘Like Baldwin said, you begin to think you are alone in this, until you read’. Nelson often pays tribute to a range of his artistic influences, including Baldwin, Barry Jenkins, Kendrick Lamar, and Zadie Smith, and today he will lead a Close Read workshop on a literary work that matters to him as an artist, and as a person.

Description: Arriving in Australia in 1989, Bob planned a six month stay. 35 years later he's still there. After teaching scuba diving on the Great Barrier Reef and Fijian Islands, Bob embarked on a varied corporate career including a stint as a successful sports franchise board member. Bob's adventures and funny stories could fill a thousand shows... Limited space, so best you book early! Why rodeo in the title? Come and find out?

Description: From Australian X Factor to the stages of Edinburgh, Frankie Stone is opening her Emotion Farm to teach about the power of emotions and how changing the sound of your voice can change the world. Farming is a term often used only for the labour of physical land but, as many humans know, there is more than one "land" that can be farmed or even conquered. Through soulful sounds Frankie takes you on an inspiring journey through their Emotion Farm.

Description: Following sold-out shows at the Adelaide Fringe, Comedy of Terrors is coming to Edinburgh. After fleeing the danger of two wars, Vida Slayman thought she was prepared for anything life could throw at her. But then she faced a battle she couldn’t flee – motherhood. Spanning stories from Beirut, San Francisco and Adelaide, Comedy of Terrors is an uplifting reminder that no matter how bad things may be, if you’ve got kids, they can always get worse. Limited tickets are available for this exclusive season of Comedy of Terrors – grab yours now.

Description: A story of love, loss and how to let go, The Stall, an original one-act play written and performed by award-winning actor Jack Twelvetree, cuts to the heart of the human experience as we follow a son navigating his way through the journey of grief. First performed at His Majesty's Theatre, Australia in 2021, this heartbreakingly raw and beautifully acted play reminds us to cherish the time we have with the people we love.

Description: From Bach to The Beatles and beyond, South Australian musician/songwriter William Jack presents a free (non-ticketed) multi-style cello recital in the heart of Edinburgh. The program includes iconic songs (by AC/DC, Bob Dylan, Fleetwood Mac and more) dismantled and reimagined for solo cello. Intertwined with original compositions from William's debut album, This Old Cello Box. There's something for everyone, with decipherable elements of worldwide folk to bluegrass and rock. William incorporates his jazz guitar background into an unconventional style of cello playing, delivering cellopickin' grooves and catchy hooks alongside intimate melodies. Don't miss this electrifying performance!

Karen takes you on her version of that journey with songs from Kirsty’s entire career from They Don’t Know in 1979 to the final album released in her lifetime Tropical Brainstorm. For most of the songs Karen will accompany herself on guitar, and for others she will sing to her band-in-a-stick, backing tracks taken from her professionally produced tribute albums. Songs will be interspersed with snippets of Kirsty’s life up to her untimely death in 2000.

Description: Set in the city slums of 1920s Australia and based on true events, Shadows of Angels sees four women recollect the part each played in a crime on one hot, volatile day. The horrific event set in motion an investigation and opened up a mystery from the past that connected these four very different individuals. Shadows of Angels explores the desperate lives and dangerous minds of female criminals, challenging ideas of gender, sexuality, poverty and crime. Featuring Fleur Murphy’s poetic language, a live original score by Kirstin Honey, and masterful direction by Iris Walshe-Howling.

Led by the living sunbeam Astrid Jorgensen, become the music legend you've always dreamed of, even if your voice is appalling! Equal parts beer, comedy and chaos, Pub Choir is the Aussie sensation that will have you belting out a song in three-part harmony with hundreds of strangers and not giving a rat's... Description: Imagine Margot Robbie mixed with Steve Irwin, that's Nikki! The controversy queen of Australian TV. She's hosted JFL at Sydney Opera House, survived a month in the jungle with Charlotte Crosby, recently had her own hit TV show. After making international headlines for her controversial show On The Spectrum, Nikki invites you to check out her box in Bad Barbie. 'F*cking hilarious' (Bert Kreischer). Title: Silly Little Things
Description: Impeccably written theatre with a biting comedic edge; SLT is an intimate hour of storytelling from your most charming, albeit dysfunctional, friend. Dive into Rosie's whirlwind journey with donuts, mullet boys, crabby neighbours and Tom Cruise, as she seeks solace in unexpected places. If you've splurged all your cash on tequila, turned to Hinge for a hug, or struggled to mend a crumbling friendship, this show will touch your heart, make you laugh and remind you of the beauty in life's ups and downs. 'It is mesmerising, and she was mighty' (TheBlurb.com.au).

This is a celebration of the other bit, of a cold, crisp departure. This is the latest creation by award-winning Australian theatre maker Stuart Bowden; a musical feast of ethereal melancholia. Praise for previous work: 'Weirdly magical' (Scotsman on Before Us). 'Master theatre maker' (Stage on Wilting in Reverse). 'Stunning' (Advertiser, Adelaide on She Was Probably Not a Robot).

Join opera and musical theatre singer, Olivia Ruggiero, for an hour of Broadway belts, West End wonders, opera classics and those earworms that you know and love from shows including Les Miserables, Anastasia, Jesus Christ Superstar, Come From Away and many more! Title: The Psychic Tests
Description: Guardian journalist Gary Nunn’s theatrical storytelling adventure into psychics, mediums and astrologers is a combination of character-driven scenes, verbatim theatre and narration. He reveals the surprising, powerful believers who hire them in secret, and the full-time sceptics who pursue them. The Psychic Tests features the funniest, most shocking and most poignant stories from his two year investigation into the psychic industry in Britain and Australia. Every story is true. ‘Nunn guides you through this world of startling truths and shocking lies. Terrific. Brave’ (Miriam Margolyes). 'An exhilarating ride of scrutiny and flair' (Jessie Tu, Sydney Morning Herald).

Description: You can’t say moist, you can’t assume a person’s gender or even if they identify as a person at all, maybe they’re a plant? What started off as a way to call out discrimination has somehow been highjacked by self-righteous people who’ve had humour-bypass surgery, virtue-signalling to grab social media likes for their fragile egos. Political correctness is ruining livelihoods and is the enemy of humour and creative thinking in general. Enough is enough. Therefore Mick Moore, JNewtz and Milton White have declared war on woke! A fast-paced show of stand-up and sketches. Adults only.

Title: Comedy for corporates: work-life balance is for losers
Description: The brave corporate professionals of the world just have to accept it. We can bear any meeting, email, call or presentation, as long as it gets us closer to priority boarding on flights that aren't to some Spanish motel. So stop fighting it, realise you chose "busy" as your whole personality and do cool stuff in the minimal time you have off. So, if you more than occasionally forget family/loved ones' birthdays and can't relate to the weed-smoking, unemployment benefit-collecting, ironic t-shirt wearing comedy from differently tax-bracketed contemporaries, this show's for you.

With three original sketch comedy shows under their belts that have toured Australia wide – they make their Edinburgh Fringe debut with Snake Oil: A Best Of Show, featuring all the highlights from their past shows. Watch as they take you on a whip fast journey blending sketch, improv and songs with a vaudevillian twist. 'Slick, in sync and hilarious' (TheatreTravels.org). 'Five stars' (Funny Tonne, ComedyFestival.com.au).

Description: Come and enjoy a night in celebration of one of the world's most beloved entertainers, the one Ms Judy Garland. My Best Judys features world-class entertainers featuring only the best tunes from the titans of the American songbook, Harold Arlen and George Gershwin amongst others. Description: A journey from Greece to Spain through art song. Spanish tenor Aitor Sorozabal and Croatian pianist Kristina Kebet present a programme featuring Manuel de Falla's famous Siete Canciones Populares and a selection of songs by Paolo Tosti among other hidden gems of the repertoire. Aitor's powerful and rich tenor voice and Kristina's crisp and elegant playing have already won over the hearts of audiences in Brussels where they reside. Join them for the first time at the Fringe as they bring to life all the passion, delicacy and beauty of these sun-drenched melodies!

Title: Là-haut (Up There)
Description: La Haut is an audiovisual show that invites the audience to immerse themselves in a one-of-a-kind world, viewing emotions of longing, home, and dream-like realities through the eyes of bird-like aeroplanes. The production is a sensory feast, combining saxophone, synths, and visuals to create a mesmerizing display of the human psyche. Sonia Killmann will include a demonstrative workshop that seeps into the performance, exploring deep listening, and the sonic world of the work, allowing the audience to feel involved in the creation process... Don't miss this opportunity to embark on a journey.

Featuring fine dining and family-friendly shows, our stunning venue in the heart of the Old Town is an unmissable attraction for Fringe audiences.

Title: I Am Not Just Me in Me – State of Nature – Procedure 01
Description: The Project, I Am Not Just Me in Me is the first theoretical-practical application procedure of the new research object of Grupo Cena 11 for 2023/2024. State of Nature: Theoretical-practical project to reconsider the practical and terminological tensions of the false behavior/language dichotomy in the light of technology as nature. I Am Not Just Me in Me proposes an anarcho-choreographic counterpoint to the concept of "Brazilian People" in Darcy Ribeiro's work, modulating the relationships between alterity, identity, behavior, and language for transduction in dance and choreography.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Nudity, Strobe lighting, Strong language/swearing

Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Deeper – Demo Version
Description: The material and immaterial body on the threshold of consciousness. 3D co-participatory scenic arts and immersive performance project. The work merges art and immersive technology to explore and question the boundaries of what we know today by "human consciousness" manifested in threshold experiences. The territories of madness, dream, and death, whether in their accidental dimension or induced within the extensive studies on psychedelia, reveal to us an extensive plasticity of what we understand today by consciousness, which also seems to resonate in the research on technologies using virtual reality. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Nudity, Scenes of a sexual nature, Scenes of sexual violence, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing

Title: Dibubuísmos
Description: Dibubuismo, by the poet Paes Loureiro is letting the spirit work in its daydreams, while the body rests floating, 'dibubuia in the river'. The video-oriented performance entitled Dibubuísmos is developed from this concept, presenting a female body that throws itself into the river and lives a flanerie in the waters of the Pará Amazon. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Artist: Marise Maués / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: As I Roved Out
Description: Journey along ancient song lines with The Bardesse, everywoman time-travelling troubadour, as your guide. Weaving together theatre, traditional Celtic folk ballads and storytelling accompanied by fiddle and guitar, Canadian multi-instrumentalist and newcomer to the Fringe, Bronwyn Claire Asha, invites you to begin your day with a delightful and immersive voyage through the history of song and story to discover just how connected we are to each other, to our earth, and to those we came before us. The future has an ancient heart – will you take up the call in remembrance of it?
Venue description: An easy-going hangout with a back room with sofa seating and afternoon movies. With a selection of board games and an array of movies, there’s plenty to do besides drink at the Brass Monkey. However, the drinks alone, which are cheaper than usual and come with a student discount, keep the bar busy and the Free Fringe Festival shows fill the cinema room and games room each afternoon.

Title: It's Magic, but is it Art?
Description: How would it feel to watch a conjuror perform in the Middle Ages, when suspected witches and sorcerers were cruelly tortured or burnt alive at the stake? What if you then travelled, via some shamanistic ritual and a shared dream through an imaginary plane… all the way to the conceptual art of today? In this modern magic show, Dimis takes you on a journey to explore the changing meaning of art and magic. He will tell stories and challenge your mind, as good art and magic must always do.

Title: Bryony Byrne: A Clown Tries to Write a Play (WIP)
Description: Bryony's done with clowning. She's going to try to write a play. Plays are what get you noticed in the UK. After all, some of our greatest playwrights have written plays... Given an infinite amount of time with a typewriter, a monkey will produce the complete works of Shakespeare... but what can a clown do in an hour? 'Joyously ramshackle, spirit-of-the-Fringe stuff' **** (Telegraph). 'A playful, surprising and very timely show' (Comedy.co.uk). British Comedy Guide Recommended Shows 2022. The Telegraph's Edinburgh Fringe Comedy Reviews: The Best Shows of 2022.

Title: Chansons: Songs and Stories from Piaf, Brel and Me
Description: Bienvenue to Chansons, the musical intercultural cabaret. ‘Soul-touching’ stories performed in ‘brilliant showmanship’ (Audience reviews) about life and passion, from Ne me quitte pas (Brel) to Milord (Piaf). Live life the French way. Experience joie de vivre. Created by award-winning musical theatre actress Stefanie Rummel. Spoken in English; sung in French, English. Accompanied by Bogdan Pieleanu, Tom Schlueter, Bob Egan. Inspires our own lives by looking at other cultures. ‘Great chansons... passionate feelings’ (Rheingauer Echo). ‘Rummel’s voice is outstanding… real moments of joie de vivre’ **** (TheReviewHub.com). ‘Fascinating’ **** (LondonTheatre1.com).

Help solve this zigzagging mystery and join Kat on a ludicrous rollercoaster journey through last night's shenanigans. Description: Romping through the joys, disappointments and semen of her 30s in Berlin, Anna stays surprisingly optimistic. In her solo stand-up hour, she celebrates German empathy, nasty sex with manners and non-judgemental feminism. Sex focused, self-deprecating, dark and upbeat, Anna turns pain into laughter and shame into solidarity. High energy, filthy, joyous, hilarious.

This show will take you on a journey to far away places you didn’t know existed – ever heard of Hy-Brasil? – and down the rabbit holes of your own backyard, all the while proving that learning and exploring can be fun. Description: Frankenstein: a timeless classic that explores the troubling themes of creation, responsibility, and morality. Featuring an international ensemble of immigrant performers based in Berlin, Germany, this production closely examines the role of social alienation within this iconic story. From the consequences of unchecked ambition to the value of empathy and the importance of moral responsibility, Berlin Open Theatre investigates the complicated world of Frankenstein with renewed vigour.

Description: A contemporary adaptation of Voltaire's Candide, this devised ensemble work depicts the optimist's journey from innocence to experience. Candide is raised in a sheltered environment and taught that everything is for the best. On leaving home, he discovers that the world is not as perfect as he thinks. He sees the harshness of life, but he never loses faith in people's goodness. Featuring colourful characters and poetic storytelling, this production from Hong Kong, by an award-winning director, is a fun and thought-provoking exploration of the human condition. Title: Hallucinations of an Artifact
Description: In response to India’s current right-wing government's project of asserting the idea of a Hindu nation, this work brings the Dancing Girl from Mohenjo-Daro (c 2300-1750 BCE) to life through dance and artificial intelligence. Through a choreographic play with the Dancing Girl, this work challenges the simplistic historical narratives attributed to it and sets up a dialogue with the inherently political act of history-writing. How does an artifact think and move for itself? Can the body of the nation in the 75th year of its independence be imagined as this irreverently playful artifact?
Artist: Mandeep Raikhy / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Maati Katha (Earth Stories)
Description: In the dangerous and magical land of Sunderbans, living is about a fragile balance: between land and water, domestic and wild, human and human, calm and storm. As each stakes claim on the other and encroaches upon the other’s space, survival is possible only through stories and beliefs. Bonbibi is said to have come to the Land of the 18 Tides to protect all beings here. But, only if we agree to her terms. When she looks away, devastation follows. In this Object Theatre performance, traditional dolls of the region tell contemporary stories of their land.
Artist: Tram Arts Trust, India / Voices from the South Showcase

Title: how long is february? a fantasy in three parts
Description:
15 years after the brutal events of February 2020 in Delhi, a nation reckons with the truth of what really happened. In parallel, there is the urgent matter of 72 arrested goats and an unfolding conspiracy.

"That which is denied must be imagined" (Sartre) Set in an imagined future and based on real events, this is a project in narrative justice delivered via the performative. Using a satirical lens, the play questions the complicity and inaction of various groups involved in the denial of justice.

Written and directed by Nisha Abdulla

Title: Sufiana: A Contemporary Kathak Presentation
Description: An abstract representation of the philosophy of Sufism in thrilling choreography. Seven professional Indian classic dancers from Delhi form intricate geometric patterns accompanied by a spectacular light show with music on the path of enlightenment, awakening, unconditional love and salvation. The dance is a stylised Kathak presentation with enchanting music specially recorded for the Fringe by Indian band Mrigya. Sufiana is influenced by great Sufi poets including Rumi, Kabeer, Bulleh Shah and Tagore. A visual treat.

The performance features powerful storytelling via music and pre-recorded performances on screen by professional actors which capture the loves, joys, growth, conflicts and compassion of the 13-year-old schoolgirl whose message of hope in secret hiding during World War Two has inspired millions. A message as relevant today as ever. 'Girish's heart-warming music will truly touch your heart' (Ashok Prema).

Title: Stanislaus and James
Description: Trieste, 1953. James and Stanislaus Joyce were once as close as two brothers can be. But when they had moved from Dublin to Trieste by 1905, they gradually grew apart. Why did their relationship not flourish? Stanislaus remained in Trieste while James relocated to Paris and then Zurich.  Stanislaus, with a mixture of envy and regret, reminisces about their ambivalent, sometimes fractious, relationship. They met in Paris for the last time in 1926. James died in 1941. Stanislaus was the addressee of the last note he wrote. He died in 1955, on the 16th of June, Bloomsday.

They care fiercely for each other and defend their independence. As they hold each other up and push each other down, the "performance" of age is unpacked as a reminder of ourselves: our worst and our best.

Title: Anna Vanosi Jazz Trio
Description: Anna Vanosi and her ensemble bring you on a journey filled with tasteful jazz, early blues standards and some Italian tunes. Drawing from the rich canon of Italian popular song as well as the American tradition, Anna Vanosi embodies the character of every song she sings, continuously drawing imagination, passion and energy from the depths of her soul. 'Eccentric, adorable, enchanting: A real life Italian diva' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).
Venue description: This stylish basement bar is Edinburgh's coolest, multiple award-winning, year-round live music venue, with a crammed programme of multi-genre music and Fringe shows running all day, every day, from 13:00 – 05:00. As well as all the independent Fringe shows hosted by the venue, you’ll hear the bar’s excellent music, with great jazz, funk, acoustic, blues and rocky sounds – and bar service to 05:00 nightly!
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Access to the basement venue is by two flights of stairs down from street level

Title: Yuriko Kotani: This Is My Work
Description: BBC New Comedy Award winner, UK-based Japanese comedian. As seen on Russell Howard’s Stand Up Central, Pls Like (BBC Three), Paul Hollywood Eats Japan (Channel 4), Mandy (BBC Two) and Sorry, I Didn’t Know (ITV). Quotes from previous work: 'Kotani has a magical way of telling a story… her imagination transforms everyday battles into something extraordinary' **** (Scotsman). 'A phenomenally feel-good show' **** (BroadwayBaby.com). 'A brilliantly performed, well-structured and wonderfully unique set. 5/5' ***** (FringeBiscuit.com).
Venue description: Located on Niddry Street, between the Royal Mile and Cowgate, Monkey Barrel Comedy presents another fantastic programme of shows from The Hive. Shows will run from 12:00 – 22:00 across its two rooms. See www.monkeybarrelcomedy.com for more information. Monkey Barrel Comedy is in the heart of Edinburgh's Old Town, with the best acts in the best rooms at the Fringe.

Title: Sun and Crystal
Description: Two shadows are dancing in a field of flowers next to a battlefield. The memories of a woman killed there – recorded by the crystal. Taken away by shadows to a place where time has stopped, the woman embarks on a journey to find it. Based on Japanese folktales, Noh, and butoh that reveal the human unconscious, this is a story about the memories of human extinction engraved in DNA. Through poetry and drama Sun and Crystal describes an apocalypse of modern civilisation. A universal contemporary myth that transcends time and borders.

Title: Colorhythm Painting Show
Description: Colorhythm Risa uses her hands, sponges, sometimes her entire body, to apply colour across the canvas from end-to-end. Her physical and facial expressions of various human emotions and feelings add further layers of depth to her performances. Fusing art and entertainment, Risa draws a story while changing the picture on a large canvas. Through her works, Risa wants to connect people and societies, and to make art more accessible to the world while expanding its potential to be more fun and more familiar.

Title: Jazz Emu: You Shouldn't Have
Description: Returning after two sell-out runs at Soho Theatre, global sensation Jazz Emu is back with his virtuoso musical spectacular. 'This is a work of genius' ***** (Telegraph). In 2016, Jazz Emu played the biggest gig he'd ever landed at the Helsinki Velodrome. But during his between-song patter, he carelessly insulted one of his biggest fans. Now he's back to clear his name and regain his former glory. Will he be able to get every single person in the world to like him? Or is it time for him to face the music?

Title: The Princess Pyunggang
Description: The Bibimbab Theatre (BT) participated and got enthusiastic applause at the 2010, 2012 and 2022 Edinburgh Festival Fringe, 2011 Brighton Cultural Olympiad, 2014 NYF, and 2011, 2017, 2018 and 2019 IYAF. The Bibimbab, taken from the name of a popular Korean dish (mixed rice), is a Korean traditional musical dedicated to integrating modern influences while honoring Korea’s rich heritage. The love story of a fool and a princess is released into a beautiful and passionate musical, dealing with the most beautiful human nature beyond the border and status.

Title: Rozarina Larsen Presents: Whitefishing
Description: Rozarina Larsen presents: White Fishing – a work-in-progress comedy about finding your authenticity. As an Asian teenager in the 80s, Rozarina was clueless of what it takes to appear cool. In this bizarre comedy of self exploration, Rozarina gets real with some of her idols throughout her journey to adulthood from Madonna to Mother Theresa to Marie Condo and faces her obsession with whiteness. Come prepared to listen to some probably not-so-woke comedy in 2023 as Rozarina unfolds her identity-crisis in her path to finding her authenticity.
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms between this venue and its sister venues 32 Below and The Pear Tree every day from 10:00 to 03:00. There's a massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, a full restaurant food selection and giant outdoor screen. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?

Title: Amanda Tovalin: Música Verde (Green Music)
Description: Música Verde (Green Music) is a live looping concert where Mexican singer/songwriter Amanda Tovalin shares her views about nature in the cities with her sonic experimentation. This technique is based on the live recording of different rhythmic and melodic sequences, phrases or loops, overlapping one on top of the other, forming a particular live arrangement that generates a truly progressive vibe in listeners – something that will undoubtedly capture your attention. Green Music: name of the material performed in this video concert, whose concept covers unusual themes within the musical mainstream.
Artist: Amanda Tovalin / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Viaje al Centro de Alhijara
Description: Audiovisual adaptation of the homonymous play based on the novel Journey to the Center of the Earth by Jules Verne, where teenagers tell us about their passage through adolescence in their Mexican communities; this is a journey inside themselves, where they show us that they are like volcanoes, that they may be apparently asleep, but inside they have a revolution about to erupt. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Artist: Pequeños Creadores Teatro / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Conquest of Bread / Conquista del Pan
Description: Conquest of Bread is a creative and critical space woven mostly by working women and domestic workers from San Juan de Abajo, Mexico, to discuss their working conditions. An invitation to act from the historical recognition of the abuses and workers' struggles carried out by their gender, the political imagination located in the present and the demand for labor justice from art and activism. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Artist: Community art collective/Lxs de Abajo, Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: 1953: The Race for the Summit
Description: "Tomorrow is a big day. Our first attempt to reach the summit. That was our plan, but mountains have their own plan." Set the night before Tenzing Norgay Sherpa made history with Sir Edmund Hillary by becoming the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest, this one-man show charts his thoughts and fears at the attempt ahead. He relives his other attempts, hampered by avalanches and snowfall until the anxiety and exhaustion transform into the exhilaration of success. Written and performed by Om Raj Raut.

Title: The Jam Society
Description: A wild and chaotic alternative extravaganza fresh from Amsterdam's theatres, featuring a dazzling parade of hilariously smart, silly and sexy international variety acts. Presented the "sweet" and "mildly inept" Daniel (by night) and accompanied by a live, high-energy and mostly harmless improv band. 'One of those wonderful Fringe experiences you'll never forget' (Scotsman). Past guests have included Lara Ricote, Zach Zucker, Elf Lyons, John Robertson, Matt Parker and Tom Walker. More info and full line-ups at www.thejamsociety.com
Warnings: Audience participation, Nudity, Scenes of a sexual nature, Strong language/swearing

Home to both Edinburgh Comedy Awards Best Comedy Show and Best Newcomer in 2022. Fourteen award nominees since 2017. Scotland’s Best Venue 2023 (Chortle Awards). Three time Scottish Comedy Awards winner. “Down there at the Monkey Barrel, there’s something in the water, and I can't stop drinking it!”

Title: Walking Songs
Description:
Once upon a time, she walked the length of Aotearoa New Zealand. To scream at the ocean, to sing at the trees, to curse the effing supplejack vine. She walked to process grief, to know alone, to remember home. While she walked, she sang.
In an intimate performance of story and songs for wandering feet, Moon's retelling of walking Te Araroa hiking trail, celebrates the power of voice, body, and being shit scared but doing it anyway. Moon’s unique and raw performance style engages audiences to embrace story, in sometimes uncomfortably intimate, sometimes darkly explosive performances.
Venue description: Greenside @ Nicolson Square is set in the heart of town, seconds from the Festival Theatre, the flashing lights of Bristo Square and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.

Title: Call Mr Robeson – A Life, with Songs
Description: One of the twentieth century’s most impressive but overlooked figures is revived in this powerful, compelling tour-de-force. When Paul Robeson, actor, singer, civil rights campaigner gets too radical and outspoken for the establishment’s liking, he is branded a traitor, harassed, and denied opportunities. This rollercoaster journey through Robeson’s remarkable life highlights how his pioneering and heroic activism led many to see him as the forerunner of the civil rights movement. Features memorable songs (including a dramatic rendition of Ol’ Man River), and Robeson’s testimony to the Un-American Activities Committee. ‘First-rate’ **** (Guardian).

Title: Just An Ordinary Lawyer
Description: As the British Empire struggles to keep its colonial possessions, Nigerian lawyer Tunji Sowande quietly breaks through multiple barriers to become Britain’s first Black judge. A fine concert singer and keen cricket follower, he muses on international politics and history as they affect the Black world from Africa to the USA and Britain, from the point of view of one who would rather watch sports, and spread love and peace through the medium of song. Recalling heroic sporting achievements alongside epoch-defining political events, Tayo Aluko delivers ‘a masterclass in performance art, research and history’ (EdFringeReview.com).

Title: Tony Pasquier
Description: Kicked out of opera school for being too much of a prima donna, Tony Pasquier took to earning his living as a singer-cum-comedian. Amongst others he's played cruise ships, holiday camps and nightclubs. He speaks of his many (usually failed) romances. One incident that still rankles concerns his archrival Brian Cleethorpes ('the man with a voice to move millions') who stole his girl – or did he?  In this show Tony comes full circle, revisiting his love of opera and trying to make sense of the rollercoaster his career has been.

Title: O Tusitala: Tellers of Tales
Description: This new one-person play by leading Samoan writer Sia Figiel vividly tells, through the voices of never-before-heard indigenous characters, the extraordinary story of Robert Louis Stevenson's household in 1890s Samoa. Through powerful monologues and magnificent music by characters from gardeners to cooks to Stevenson himself, this is a striking portrayal of a fascinating history exploring Stevenson's engagement with Samoan politics and culture, his adventures in agriculture and the bonds he formed with people who knew him not as a famous writer, but as an employer, a political ally, a high chief and friend.

Title: Baked Shakespeare: As You Like It
Description: Popular South African production, Baked Shakespeare, is coming to the Edinburgh Fringe! Baked Shakespeare – a group of professionally trained actors – performing Shakespeare how you have never seen it before. As You Like It is a classic Shakespearean comedy, following the love story between Rosalind and Orlando, and the freedom they find in the Forest of Arden. The show plays with gender identity, feminism, and wrestling. Fun fact – Rosalind has the most lines of any woman in a Shakespeare play.

Title: Still Connecting…
Description: A collaborative multimedia project where African students across the diaspora navigate time zones, rising data costs, and perpetually loading screens in the name of connection. This is an ongoing investigation of the shifting political and social realities Africans navigate within digital spaces. Portions of this project have been made available to the public to experiment, to play, and to grow the project. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Artist: Faye Kabali-Kagwa / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Ethnoscape
Description: Ethnoscape is an audio-visual interpretation of five turbulent moments in South Africa's history. Beginning with the 17th century Dutch arrival, through to the first democratic elections of the early 1990s, Elvis Sibeko draws from what might've been heard and seen by those who lived through the events. Through (re)imagination and translation of sounds and images, the audience is invited on a virtual journey and unique experience where the past and present overlaps.
Artist: Elvis Sibeko Studios / Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: AnotherKind
Description: AnotherKind is a collaborative theatre project presented by South African theatre-makers, performers, sound, collage and video artists. It draws from Amy Louise Wilson’s award-winning play Another Kind of Dying which tells the story of a young man from rural Eastern Cape who moves to Johannesburg after the death of his father. An unusual archive which documents another kind of process: a meeting of theatre rehearsals, text fragments, video and sound experiments which explode in a playful, poetic and political collaboration. Featuring Aphiwe Livi. Part of Voices from the South Showcase.
Artist: Amy Louise Wilson, Aphiwe Livi, Voices from the South Showcase
Venue description: Online venue hosting Voices from the South Showcase.

Title: Twenty Hamsters
Description: Jamie Keddie: Twenty Hamsters. Despite his strong and very masculine Scottish accent, Jamie Keddie was actually born in England. Unfortunately, when his peers discovered this dirty secret, he was banished and forced to go south of the border. Now, with 20 hamsters under his belt and a pocketful of reasons never to return, he's back for 60 minutes of unforgettable comedy-infused storytelling. You will laugh at the Terrifying Tale of Big Dilla. You will gasp at That Unspeakable Thing I Once Saw in Edinburgh. You will go home wiser after Cow Pats in Holyrood Park.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House

Title: Fake Jews
Description: A hilarious new split-hour show featuring stand-up comedy from Luke Messina Meginsky (USA) and James Regal (UK), two of the Barcelona scene's most prolific comedians. James and Luke come from Jewish families but have never practiced Judaism at all. Watch them attempt to reconcile their current lives with the weight of their cultural past, take a surreal look at 21st century antisemitism, plus do some light-hearted stuff about hip-hop and dating in your early 40s. Fake Jews is for anyone who simultaneously feels like a member and an outsider of any community.
Warnings: Contains distressing or potentially triggering themes, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: We welcome you to The Raging Bull, an Edinburgh cocktail bar famous for its coffee cocktails. Our cosy bar is inspired by the eccentric yet good-natured fellow, who has become accustomed to drinking his cocktails in comfortable and stylish surroundings. So expect rustic walls, marble tables, natural foliage and walls adorned with pictures of the handsome Bull when you visit us, plus free Fringe shows downstairs daily.
